# Maester Packs that ship with Maester

Each folder here is a [Maester Pack](https://maester.dev/docs/packs) that is part of the Maester module:
a `maester-pack.json`, its suites of native tests, and its helpers and connectors.

- The build copies this folder to `packs/` in the module. A pack loads into its own private module from
  its folder; it is not compiled into `Maester.psm1`.
- A pack here is trusted as the module is: it needs no lock entry and no approval. It runs when its
  manifest says `"EnabledByDefault": true` unless the Maester config turns it off with
  `Packs: [{ "Id": "<id>", "Enabled": false }]`, and the other way round.
- Its ID is `maester.<name>`. Its `Code` is its own, such as `ZTA`. Because it is part of Maester, its test IDs
  have no `MP.` prefix: they are `ZTA.<n>` (or `ZTA` for a family), and its suite IDs start with `ZTA`. The code
  is added to the reserved prefixes in `powershell/assets/MaesterTestSchema.psd1`, so custom tests cannot use it. A pack installed later may not take a code that overlaps it. Its rows in the results have `Source = Custom` and a `Package`, so they never count as
  Maester's own checks.
- PowerShell Gallery modules it declares in `Uses.Modules` are pinned to one version. Users save them with
  `Install-MtPack <id>`, which records each module's digest in `maester-packs.lock.json`.

Check a pack with `Test-MtPack ./packs/<name> -Official` and run its tests with `Invoke-MtTest -Path ./packs/<name>`.

---
title: Writing a pack
sidebar_position: 2
description: Create, check and publish a Maester Pack, with its manifest, tests, helpers and connector.
---

# Writing a pack

:::tip Guided setup
To make a pack without writing the files by hand, use the guided setup at
[packs.maester.cloud/publish](https://packs.maester.cloud/publish). It copies the
[demo pack](https://github.com/maester365/maester-pack-demo) into a repository of yours, or starts from an empty one,
and fills in the manifest, the pack's Guide, its tests and its banner from a form. Then it releases the pack and
publishes it. It writes the same files this page describes, so you can change any of them later by hand.
:::

A pack is a folder with a `maester-pack.json`. Create one with `New-MtPack`:

```powershell
New-MtPack -Path ./maester-google-workspace -Id contoso.google-workspace -Code CNT -Connector
Test-MtPack ./maester-google-workspace
Invoke-MtTest -Path ./maester-google-workspace
```

`Invoke-MtTest -Path` runs the pack from its folder, with its helpers and connector, and reloads it on every call.
`Test-MtPack` runs every check `Install-MtPack` runs, without installing: use it in the pack's own CI.

```text
maester-google-workspace/
  maester-pack.json
  README.md
  tests/
    suite.json
    Test.MP.CNT.1001.ps1
    Test.MP.CNT.1001.md
  helpers/
    Get-CntWorkspaceSetting.ps1
  connector/
    Connect-CntGoogleWorkspace.ps1
```

To share the pack, push the folder to a GitHub repository owned by the publisher and create a release. A release made
[immutable](https://docs.github.com/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/about-releases) starts its
cooldown when it is published; any other release starts it when each user first sees it. To have it listed where
people look for packs, see [Publishing your pack](#publishing-your-pack).

## The manifest

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://maester.dev/schemas/maester-pack-1.0.json",
  "Id": "contoso.google-workspace",
  "Name": "Google Workspace checks",
  "Description": "Checks the security settings of a Google Workspace tenant.",
  "Version": "1.2.0",
  "Publisher": "contoso",
  "License": "MIT",
  "RequiresMaester": ">=3.0",
  "Code": "CNT",
  "Suites": ["tests"],
  "Helpers": ["helpers"],
  "Connectors": [
    {
      "Service": "CNT.GoogleWorkspace",
      "DisplayName": "Google Workspace",
      "File": "connector/Connect-CntGoogleWorkspace.ps1",
      "Connect": "Connect-CntGoogleWorkspace",
      "Test": "Test-CntGoogleWorkspace",
      "Disconnect": "Disconnect-CntGoogleWorkspace"
    }
  ],
  "Uses": {
    "Services": ["CNT.GoogleWorkspace"],
    "GraphScopes": [],
    "TenantWrites": [],
    "Network": ["admin.googleapis.com", "oauth2.googleapis.com"],
    "Modules": [ { "Name": "GoogleWorkspaceTools", "Version": "1.4.2" } ]
  }
}
```

| Key | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `$schema` | `https://maester.dev/schemas/maester-pack-1.0.json`, so editors such as VS Code check the manifest as you type. Maester checks it again when the pack is installed and loaded. |
| `Id` | `<publisher>.<name>` in lower case. The publisher is the GitHub user or organisation that owns the repository; a pack whose publisher is not the repository owner is refused. |
| `Guid` | Required. A GUID that identifies the pack for good, such as `d1e2db80-6c27-4cb6-9389-2edf0a898d23`; `New-MtPack` makes one. Keep it, and the code, for every version of the pack: `Update-MtPack` refuses a release whose Guid or code changed. A pack with a new code is a new pack, with a new Guid. |
| `Version` | A semantic version, such as `1.2.0`. |
| `RequiresMaester` | The Maester versions the pack works with, such as `>=3.0`. Add an upper bound, such as `>=3.0 <4.0`, only if you know a later version breaks the pack. A pack that needs a newer Maester reports `RequiresNewerMaester`. `New-MtPack` fills in the version you made the pack with. |
| `Code` | The start of every test ID of the pack: `CNT` gives `MP.CNT.1001`. Two to ten letters or digits, starting with a letter. A publisher with several packs can group them with up to three parts separated by dots, such as `CNT.GWS` for `MP.CNT.GWS.1001`. No two installed packs may share a code, or have one code that starts with the other (`CNT` and `CNT.GWS`), so `Install-MtPack` refuses the second one. Any code is allowed, but pick one that the [Maester Packs site](https://packs.maester.cloud) does not list as claimed, so people can install your pack next to others. |
| `Suites` | Folders of native tests. Each needs a `suite.json` whose `Id` is the code or starts with it, such as `CNT.GoogleWorkspace`. |
| `Helpers` | Folders of `.ps1` files that hold functions the tests call. |
| `Connectors` | Services the pack connects to (below). |
| `Uses` | What the pack reaches, shown when it is installed. An unknown key under `Uses` is an error, so a pack cannot hide what it reaches behind a key an older Maester does not show. |
| `Uses.Modules` | PowerShell Gallery modules, each pinned to one exact `Version`. Maester saves them into its own store and checks their files before every load. A module the user installs themselves can only be run in a separate process: `{ "Name": "X", "MinimumVersion": "2.0.0", "Install": "User", "Process": "Child" }`. |
| `Requires.Packs` | Other packs this one needs: `{ "Id": "contoso.base", "Source": "contoso/maester-base", "Version": ">=1.0" }`. They are installed first, with their own approval. |
| `Exports` | Functions of this pack that packs requiring it may call. |
| `Pricing` | `Free` (the default) or `Paid`, for a pack that needs a paid product or subscription to be useful. The pack index shows it; Maester does not act on it. |
| `Banner` | An image in the pack that the pack index shows when it features the pack. See [Banner image](#banner-image). |
| `Guide` | A JSON file in the pack that says how to install, connect and run it, for its page on the pack index. See [The pack page](#the-pack-page). |
| `EnabledByDefault` | For a pack that ships with Maester: `false` to leave it off until the config turns it on. |

## Banner image

A banner is optional. When the maintainers feature a pack on [packs.maester.cloud](https://packs.maester.cloud), the
card shows the banner beside the pack's description; without one, the card shows the pack's code and name on a dark
background.

- **File:** `.png`, `.jpg` or `.webp`, at most 1 MB, inside the pack, for example `"Banner": "assets/banner.png"`.
  The index reads the type from the file's contents, not its name, and SVG is refused. A banner that fails these
  checks is left out and the card falls back to the code and name.
- **Size:** 1200 × 630 pixels (the 1.91:1 shape of a social preview). Another size is cropped to fill that shape.
- **Shown small:** about 600 pixels wide on a desktop and 340 on a phone. Use at most eight words of text, set large,
  and keep it away from the edges.
- **Your own brand.** Use another company's logo only for a pack built on that company's product, and only with its
  permission. Don't add words such as "Official" or "Verified": the index shows its own badges, and a banner that
  suggests an endorsement it doesn't have can get the pack removed.
- **No secrets or real data:** a screenshot must not show a real tenant, user or key.

### Making one with an AI image tool

Any image tool that takes a text prompt can make a banner. Image tools often misspell words, so check every letter,
or ask for an image with no text and add the title yourself in an editor. Fill in the parts in angle brackets:

```text
A wide banner image, 1200 x 630 pixels, for a software add-on called "<pack name>".
It checks the security settings of <service, for example Google Workspace> for IT administrators.
Style: clean, modern, flat illustration on a <dark navy / deep teal / near-black> gradient background,
with a simple abstract motif suggesting <what the pack checks, for example identity, email, devices>.
Text: the title "<pack name>" in large, bold, white sans-serif letters on the left,
and the line "<one short phrase, at most six words>" below it in smaller letters.
Leave a margin of at least 60 pixels on every side. No other text, no logos, no people,
no photos of screens, no badges or seals.
```

For an image without text, replace the `Text:` line with `No text at all; leave the left half plain for a title.`

## The pack page

Every pack's page on [packs.maester.cloud](https://packs.maester.cloud) has the same sections: Install, Connect,
Run, App-only, Tests, Security and Support. The index fills what it can from the manifest:

- the modules in `Uses.Modules`, with the line that installs each one;
- the Graph permissions in `Uses.GraphScopes`, which an app needs to run the pack app-only;
- the tests, with their products, from `Suites` (and `Catalog` for a family test that expands when it runs).

The rest comes from the Guide, a JSON file in the pack named by the manifest's `Guide` key, such as
`"Guide": "maester-pack.guide.json"`. Its schema is
[maester-pack-guide-1.0.json](https://maester.dev/schemas/maester-pack-guide-1.0.json); add it as `$schema` so
editors check the file as you type. Commands in it are shown as text and never run. A short example:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://maester.dev/schemas/maester-pack-guide-1.0.json",
  "Summary": "Checks the security settings of Google Workspace.",
  "Prerequisites": [{ "Text": "A Google Workspace super admin account." }],
  "Connect": { "Steps": [{ "Text": "Connect Maester, then sign in to Google when asked", "Command": "Connect-Maester" }] },
  "Run": {
    "Commands": [{ "Text": "Only this pack", "Command": "Invoke-Maester -Pack CNT -SkipBuiltIn" }],
    "Options": [{ "Name": "GoogleWorkspace.Customer", "Default": "my_customer", "Text": "The customer ID to read." }]
  },
  "AppOnly": { "Supported": true, "Methods": { "Certificate": true, "ClientSecret": true }, "Text": "Use a service account key." },
  "Screenshots": [{ "Path": "assets/report.png", "Caption": "The pack's results in the Maester report" }],
  "Support": { "Pack": "https://github.com/contoso/maester-google-workspace/issues" }
}
```

Maester checks that the Guide is a JSON object and that its screenshots (at most six) are `.png`, `.jpg` or `.webp`
paths inside the pack. Like the banner, a screenshot that really is an image of at most 1 MB is not counted as
binary content. Any section can end with `"More": "<https link>"` to your own documentation. The
[Zero Trust Assessment pack's guide](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/packs/zero-trust-assessment/maester-pack.guide.json)
is a full example.

## Tests and helpers

A pack's tests are [native tests](../writing-tests/index.mdx) with IDs `MP.<Code>.<n>`, or `MP.<Code>` for a family whose instances add their own part. (Packs that ship with
Maester are part of it and drop the `MP.`: the Zero Trust Assessment pack's tests are `ZTA.<n>`.) Every `.ps1` in a suite
or helper folder holds only functions: code outside a function is refused, because it would run while the pack
loads. A pack loads into a private module of its own, so its tests can call its helpers and Maester's exported
commands. One pack does not see another pack's functions unless it requires that pack and the pack lists them in
`Exports`. This keeps cooperating packs from colliding; it is not a security boundary, because code in the same
PowerShell process can reach anything in it (see [Pack security](./security.md)).

The scan flags, and raises the risk of, what a reviewer should look at: binary files, dynamic code
(`Invoke-Expression`, `[scriptblock]::Create`), starting processes, requests to hosts that `Uses.Network` does not
list, and module imports that `Uses.Modules` does not list.

## Showing a long-running test's output and progress

A test that runs a tool for a long time, such as an assessment in another PowerShell process, can show the person
running Maester what the tool is doing while it runs. In the full-screen dashboard both go into a box in the main
column; in the compact layout, CI and redirected output they are written to the console, indented.

- `Write-MtTestOutput` shows the tool's log. `-Title` opens the box, each line
  scrolls into it, `-Progress` pins a changing line at the bottom, and `-Complete` closes it (Maester closes it when
  the test ends).
- `Write-MtTestProgress` shows where the tool is, as a header at the top of
  the box: the stage (`-Stage`, `-StageNumber`, `-StageCount`), a bar of the items done (`-Completed`, `-Total`,
  `-Failed`, `-Running`), what it is working on (`-Current`, `-Status`), and the errors it reported
  (`-ErrorMessage`), which the box also counts. With `-Stages` (the names of all the stages) the stages are drawn
  as a track, like the phases of a Maester run. With `-Items` (each with `Id`, and optionally `Title`, `Status`,
  `Detail` and `Seconds`) the box lists the items running and those that finished, with their result and time,
  the way the dashboard lists Maester's own tests; outside the dashboard each finished item is written once. Each
  call replaces the progress before it, so pass everything you know each time; a call with only `-ErrorMessage`
  keeps the progress.
- When the tool runs tests of its own, `-Results` (`Passed`, `Failed`, `Error`, `Investigate`, `Skipped`,
  `Running`, `Total` and optionally `Name`) and `-Groups` (the same counts with a `Name` each, such as the pillars
  of an assessment, with `-GroupLabel 'Zero Trust Pillars'`) show them in the dashboard in place of Maester's own while the
  box is open: in the Results panel and the result blocks, and where the products are listed. The times of the
  items that finished go into the Pace graph next to the logo and the Slowest panel.

```powershell
Write-MtTestOutput -Title 'Collecting the tenant data'
Write-MtTestProgress -Stage 'Exporting' -StageNumber 1 -StageCount 3 -Completed 12 -Total 40 -Running 2 -Current 'Users', 'Groups'
Write-MtTestProgress -ErrorMessage 'The export of Devices failed: Forbidden'
```

A tool in another process does not need to call Maester to report its progress. Pipe its output to
`Write-MtTestOutput`, and have it write lines of this form to standard output, from any language:

```text
##maester[progress] {"stages":["Export","Tests","Report"],"stageNumber":1,"stage":"Exporting","completed":12,"total":40,"failed":1,"items":[{"id":"Users","detail":"page 3","seconds":12},{"id":"Groups","status":"Passed","seconds":4.2}]}
##maester[progress] {"stage":"Running tests","results":{"passed":80,"failed":12,"running":4,"total":300},"groupLabel":"Zero Trust Pillars","groups":[{"name":"Identity","passed":50,"failed":8,"total":120}]}
##maester[error] The export of Devices failed: Forbidden
```

These lines set the header instead of showing in the log. The JSON object takes the names of the parameters of
`Write-MtTestProgress` in any case (`error` for `-ErrorMessage`), and leaves out what it does not know. Write a
`progress` line when something changes (at most a few times a second): each one is drawn. A line that cannot be read is dropped.

The [Zero Trust Assessment pack](./zero-trust-assessment.md) is a worked example: its child process reads the
progress the assessment keeps and the progress logs it writes, once a second, and writes these lines (see
`Invoke-MtZtaCollection` in `packs/zero-trust-assessment/tests/Test.ZTA.ps1`).

## Connectors

A connector adds a service to Maester. Its file holds a `Connect` and a `Test` function, and optionally
`Disconnect`, `Renew` and `Describe`:

```powershell
function Connect-CntGoogleWorkspace {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([string] $Domain, [string] $CredentialPath)

    $token = Get-CntAccessToken -Domain $Domain -CredentialPath $CredentialPath
    Set-MtConnectionState -Value @{ Token = $token.AccessToken; ExpiresOn = $token.ExpiresOn } -Tenant $Domain
}

function Test-CntGoogleWorkspace {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()
    [bool](Get-MtConnectionState)
}
```

- `Connect-Maester -Service CNT.GoogleWorkspace` calls `Connect` with the parameters it has from `-ServiceSetting`,
  `MAESTER_CNT_GOOGLEWORKSPACE_<PARAMETER>` and `Connections.CNT.GoogleWorkspace` in the config.
- `Set-MtConnectionState` keeps what the tests need for the PowerShell session only; `Get-MtConnectionState`
  reads it back in a test or helper. A pack can read its own connection and those of packs it requires, never
  another pack's.
- `Test` decides whether the tests that need the service run. With `ExpiresOn` in the state, Maester calls `Renew`
  shortly before it expires.
- The service name is `<Code>.<Name>`. Tests declare it like any service: `Service = 'CNT.GoogleWorkspace'`.
  `"OptIn": true` makes its tests not run, rather than skipped, while it is not connected.

## Publishing your pack

Once the pack has a release, anyone can install it from its repository with `Install-MtPack <owner>/<repo>`. To
help people find it, list it on a pack index: a site that collects packs, checks them and shows each one's page.
An index only lists a pack. People still install it straight from your repository, and Maester runs the same checks
at install whichever site they found it on.

### Maester Packs

[packs.maester.cloud](https://packs.maester.cloud/) is the index the Maester team runs. To list a pack there:

1. Go to [packs.maester.cloud/publish](https://packs.maester.cloud/publish) and choose
   **Yes, I have a pack repository**.
2. Sign in with GitHub as an admin of the repository. The repository must be public; private and internal
   repositories are never listed.
3. Pick the repository, and the folder if the pack is not at its root, then press **Check**. It reads the latest
   release and its `maester-pack.json`, and says what to fix.
4. Press **Publish**. The site registers the pack's `Guid` and `Code` to the repository's owner, so nobody else can
   publish a pack with them, and queues the pack.

Within about ten minutes the index runs `Test-MtPack`'s checks and its security scan on the release and lists the
pack, with its page at `/p/<code>`. If the pack is not listed, its status page at `/status/<owner>/<repo>` says why
and what to fix. Every later release is picked up on its own, so you publish only once. **My Packs** on the site
shows your packs and how many tenants run them, and lets you hide one from the site for a while.

function Get-MtZtaInstance {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns one ZTA instance per result of the Microsoft Zero Trust Assessment.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Instance source of the ZTA family. Reads the assessment's ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.json from the
    ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath setting when one is set (import), otherwise runs the assessment in a child
    PowerShell process (collect), then returns one instance per test result. Skips the whole family, with the
    reason, when neither is possible.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param()

    $reportPath = [string](Get-MtSetting -Name 'ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath' -Default '')
    $collected = $null
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($reportPath)) {
        $collected = Invoke-MtZtaCollection
        $reportPath = $collected.ReportPath
    }

    try {
        $report = Read-MtZtaReport -Path $reportPath
        $context = Get-MgContext
        if ($context -and $context.TenantId -and $report.TenantId -and $report.TenantId -ne $context.TenantId) {
            Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason "The Zero Trust Assessment report at $reportPath is for tenant $($report.TenantId), but Maester is connected to tenant $($context.TenantId)."
        }

        $maxAgeDays = [int](Get-MtSetting -Name 'ZeroTrustAssessment.MaxReportAgeDays' -Default 7)
        # ConvertFrom-Json reads the ISO date as a DateTime already; text is parsed invariantly, never in the current culture.
        $executedAt = [datetime]::MinValue
        $hasDate = if ($report.ExecutedAt -is [datetime]) { $executedAt = $report.ExecutedAt; $true }
        elseif ($report.ExecutedAt -is [datetimeoffset]) { $executedAt = $report.ExecutedAt.UtcDateTime; $true }
        else {
            [datetime]::TryParse([string]$report.ExecutedAt, [cultureinfo]::InvariantCulture,
                [System.Globalization.DateTimeStyles]::AdjustToUniversal -bor [System.Globalization.DateTimeStyles]::AssumeUniversal, [ref]$executedAt)
        }
        if ($maxAgeDays -gt 0 -and $hasDate -and $executedAt.ToUniversalTime() -lt [datetime]::UtcNow.AddDays(-$maxAgeDays)) {
            Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason "The Zero Trust Assessment report at $reportPath was written on $($executedAt.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd')), more than $maxAgeDays days ago. Run Invoke-ZtAssessment again, or raise the ZeroTrustAssessment.MaxReportAgeDays setting."
        }

        Add-MtZtaReportAttachment -ReportPath $reportPath
        ConvertTo-MtZtaInstance -Report $report
    } finally {
        # A collection into a temporary folder leaves nothing behind: the export holds raw tenant data.
        if ($collected -and $collected.Temporary -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $collected.OutputPath)) {
            Remove-Item -LiteralPath $collected.OutputPath -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        }
    }
}

function Add-MtZtaReportAttachment {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Embeds the assessment's own HTML report in the Maester report, opened with one click.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The assessment writes ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html in the folder given to Invoke-ZtAssessment -Path, beside
    its zt-export folder. It is read before a temporary output folder is deleted. Nothing is attached when the
    report is not there (an imported report file copied on its own), when the ZeroTrustAssessment.EmbedReport
    setting is false, or on a Maester version without Add-MtReportAttachment.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        # The report file, the assessment's output folder, or its zt-export folder.
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $ReportPath
    )

    if (-not [bool](Get-MtSetting -Name 'ZeroTrustAssessment.EmbedReport' -Default $true)) { return }
    if (-not (Get-Command -Name Add-MtReportAttachment -ErrorAction Ignore)) { return }

    $folder = if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $ReportPath -PathType Container) { $ReportPath } else { Split-Path -Path $ReportPath -Parent }
    if (-not $folder) { return }
    $html = @(
        (Join-Path $folder 'ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html'),
        (Join-Path (Split-Path -Path $folder -Parent) 'ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html')
    ) | Where-Object { $_ -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $_ -PathType Leaf) } | Select-Object -First 1
    if ($html) {
        Add-MtReportAttachment -Name 'Zero Trust Assessment' -Path $html
    } else {
        Write-Verbose "No ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html next to $ReportPath, so the assessment's own report is not embedded."
    }
}

function Read-MtZtaReport {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Reads ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.json from a file, or from a folder the assessment wrote.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param(
        # The report file, the assessment's output folder, or its zt-export folder.
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Path
    )

    $file = $Path
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path -PathType Container) {
        $file = @(
            (Join-Path $Path 'ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.json'),
            (Join-Path -Path $Path -ChildPath 'zt-export' -AdditionalChildPath 'ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.json')
        ) | Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath $_ -PathType Leaf } | Select-Object -First 1
    }
    if (-not $file -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $file -PathType Leaf)) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason "No Zero Trust Assessment report was found at $Path. Point the ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath setting at ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.json, or clear it to let Maester run the assessment."
    }

    $report = Get-Content -LiteralPath $file -Raw -Encoding utf8 | ConvertFrom-Json -Depth 20
    if (-not $report.PSObject.Properties['Tests']) {
        throw "$file is not a Zero Trust Assessment report: it has no Tests list."
    }
    $report
}

This section lists baseline policy changes that affect current [BOD 25-01 Required Configurations](https://www.cisa.gov/resources-tools/services/bod-25-01-implementing-secure-practices-cloud-services-required-configurations).

#### Additions

* MS.AAD.3.5v2 (SHALL) - Requires the SMS, voice call, and email one-time passcode (OTP) authentication methods to be disabled, since they are the weakest authenticators. This version removes the prior dependency on the Authentication Methods Manage Migration feature being set to Migration Complete (MS.AAD.3.4v1), so the policy is now evaluated independently.
* MS.AAD.9.1v1 (SHALL) - New policy requiring risky AI agents to be blocked. AI agents can access tenant resources and act autonomously, so blocking agents that exhibit risky behavior reduces the risk of unauthorized access and automated misuse. Requires a Microsoft Entra ID P2 license and either Microsoft Agent 365 or Microsoft 365 E7. Not applicable to GCC High and DoD tenants.
* MS.SHAREPOINT.1.3v1 (SHALL) - Requires external sharing to be restricted to approved external domains and/or users in approved security groups, preventing sharing with unknown organizations and individuals. Only applies when the external sharing slider is not set to Only people in your organization or Existing guests.
* MS.SHAREPOINT.3.1v1 (SHALL) - Requires expiration for "Anyone" links to be set to 30 days or less, preventing indefinite access through shared links. Only applies when the external sharing slider is set to Anyone.
* MS.SHAREPOINT.3.2v1 (SHALL) - Requires file and folder permissions for links to be set to view only, preventing anonymous file changes. Only applies when the external sharing slider is set to Anyone.
* MS.SHAREPOINT.3.3v2 (SHALL) - Requires reauthentication for people who use a verification code to be set to 30 days or less, preventing sustained access to documents. Policy version bumped to v2 because the setting can now also be configured when the external sharing slider is set to Existing guests.
* MS.SECURITYSUITE.1.1v1 (SHALL) - Requires emails with click-to-run file attachments to be blocked, including at a minimum .exe, .cmd, and .vbe files. Replaces the preset security policy requirements formerly in MS.DEFENDER.1.1v1 - MS.DEFENDER.1.5v1.
* MS.SECURITYSUITE.1.2v1 (SHALL) - Requires email scanning to be capable of reviewing emails after delivery, so messages retroactively identified as malware can be removed from mailboxes. Replaces the preset security policy requirements formerly in MS.DEFENDER.1.1v1 - MS.DEFENDER.1.5v1.
* MS.SECURITYSUITE.1.3v1 (SHALL) - Requires emails identified as containing malware to be quarantined or dropped. Replaces the preset security policy requirements formerly in MS.DEFENDER.1.1v1 - MS.DEFENDER.1.5v1.
* MS.SECURITYSUITE.3.1v1 (SHALL) - Requires a DLP policy that protects PII and sensitive information as defined by the agency, blocking at a minimum credit card numbers, U.S. ITINs, and U.S. SSNs. Replaces MS.DEFENDER.4.1v2.
* MS.SECURITYSUITE.4.1v1 (SHALL) - Requires a minimum set of alerts to be enabled so potentially malicious or service-impacting events are brought to administrators' attention. Replaces MS.DEFENDER.5.1v1.
* MS.SECURITYSUITE.5.1v1 (SHALL) - Requires unified audit logging to be enabled so agencies have visibility into user actions during incident response. Replaces MS.DEFENDER.6.1v1.
* MS.SECURITYSUITE.6.1v1 (SHALL) - Requires emails detected as spam and phishing to not be delivered to the user's inbox, reducing exposure to malicious links and attachments.
* MS.SECURITYSUITE.6.2v1 (SHALL) - Requires that allowed domains not be added to inbound anti-spam protection policies. Allowed senders may still be added.

#### Removals

* MS.DEFENDER.1.1v1, MS.DEFENDER.1.2v1, MS.DEFENDER.1.3v1, MS.DEFENDER.1.4v1, MS.DEFENDER.1.5v1, MS.DEFENDER.4.1v2, MS.DEFENDER.5.1v1, MS.DEFENDER.6.1v1 (SHALL) - The Microsoft Defender baseline has been retired and its policies reworked into the new Security Suite baseline (see Additions above). See the [policy migration mapping](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/blob/v2.0.0/PowerShell/ScubaGear/mappings/scuba-baseline-policy-migrations.csv) for where each policy moved, and [removedpolicies.md](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/blob/v2.0.0/PowerShell/ScubaGear/baselines/removedpolicies.md) for removal rationale.

#### Updates

* MS.AAD.3.2v2 (SHALL) - Policy version bumped to v2 because the policy was decoupled from MS.AAD.3.1v1. It previously applied only "if phishing-resistant MFA has not been enforced"; it now requires that MFA be enforced for all users, independent of MS.AAD.3.1v1.
* MS.EXO.2.2v3 (SHALL) - Policy version bumped to v3 to allow SPF soft fail. Either hardfail (`-all`) or softfail (`~all`) may now be used to comply; previously only hardfail was accepted.

# Dependencies

Before [executing](../execution/execution.md) ScubaGear, its dependencies must be installed:

```powershell
# Install the minimum required dependencies
Install-ScubaDependencies
```

> **Note**: ScubaGear utilizes several libraries from Microsoft to read data about their product configurations.  At least one of these libraries is tied to PowerShell 5.  Until Microsoft updates their library, ScubaGear will continue to use PowerShell 5.  As this version is only available on Windows, ScubaGear will only run on Windows.

> **Note**: `Install-ScubaDependencies` was previously named `Initialize-SCuBA`. The old name is retained as a backward-compatible alias, so existing scripts continue to work.

`Install-ScubaDependencies` will install the modules in the [PowerShell Module Dependencies](#powershell-module-dependencies) section on your system. It will also install [OPA](https://www.openpolicyagent.org).

> **Note**: The `Install-ScubaDependencies` cmdlet creates a `.scubagear` folder in the users home directory.  This is where it stores OPA and any other related files.

## PowerShell Module Dependencies

The following PowerShell modules are required for ScubaGear to function properly. These modules and their version constraints are defined in [RequiredVersions.ps1](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/blob/main/PowerShell/ScubaGear/RequiredVersions.ps1):

| Module Name                                   | Minimum Version | Maximum Version  | Purpose                                      |
|:---------------------------------------------:|:---------------:|:----------------:|:---------------------------------------------|
| Microsoft.Graph.Authentication |           2.0.0 |           2.25.0 | Microsoft Graph API authentication |
| powershell-yaml |           0.4.2 |           0.4.12 | YAML file processing and configuration management |

> **Note**: SharePoint and PowerPlatform data are now retrieved via REST API and no longer require Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell or PnP.PowerShell modules.

> **Note**: The maximum versions are updated to the latest available versions on a scheduled basis.

## OPA Installation

Normally, the `Install-ScubaDependencies` cmdlet installs OPA.  This can be verified by looking for the OPA executable file in `C:\Users\johndoe\.scubagear\Tools`.  If it failed to do so, or you set a parameter to prevent it from doing so, you can install OPA separately.

Try this cmdlet first:

```powershell
# Download OPA
Install-OPAforSCuBA
```

# ScubaGear Cached Execution

## Overview

`Invoke-SCuBACached` is a specialized version of the main ScubaGear function designed for development and testing workflows. It differs from `Invoke-SCuBA` in two key ways:

### Output Folder Structure

**`Invoke-SCuBA`** creates a timestamped subfolder:

```text
OutPath\
  └── M365BaselineConformance_2025_11_18_14_30_45\
      ├── ProviderSettingsExport.json
      ├── ScubaResults_abc123.json
      └── BaselineReports.html
```

**`Invoke-SCuBACached`** places output files directly in the specified path:

```textThe most important parameter that distinguishes
OutPath\
  ├── ProviderSettingsExport.json
  ├── ScubaResults_abc123.json
  └── BaselineReports.html
```

This simplified structure makes iterative development easier—you can run full mode once to export provider data, then repeatedly run in cached mode without adjusting the `OutPath` parameter.

### Execution Modes

`Invoke-SCuBACached` supports two distinct execution modes:

1. **Full mode** (`-ExportProvider $true`, default) - Authenticates, exports provider data, runs Rego analysis, and generates reports (similar to `Invoke-SCuBA` but outputs directly to `OutPath` without creating a timestamped subfolder)
2. **Cached mode** (`-ExportProvider $false`) - Skips data collection and authentication, running analysis only on previously exported provider JSON files

This function is particularly useful for:

- Rego policy development and testing
- Re-running analysis on previously collected data without re-authentication

##### docs/installation/DownloadAndInstall.md
# Getting started
> [!IMPORTANT]
> Use of this tool requires access to an internet browser for initial setup
> and to view the html report output.
Setting up to run ScubaGoggles as a user for the first time involves the following steps:
1. Installing [Python 3](https://www.python.org/) on your system.
2. (Optional) Creating and activating a Python virtual environment.
3. Downloading the latest release.
4. Installing ScubaGoggles and dependencies into the Python environment.
5. Running `scubagoggles setup` to specify the output directory, the location of the
   OPA executable, and the credentials file.  By default, the setup will
   download the Open Policy Agent (OPA) executable for you.
6. Creating a Google OAuth credential file, unless you'll be using a Google
   service account.
Each of the above steps is detailed in the following sections.
## Installing Python 3
Running ScubaGoggles requires Python 3.11 or higher.  If Python is not installed
in your environment, please visit the [Python website](https://www.python.org/)
for instructions on how to download and install Python.
A 64-bit operating system is required.  While Python will run in a 32-bit
environment, the Open Policy Agent (OPA) required for ScubaGoggles is only
available on 64-bit platforms.
Depending on the operating system, the command to invoke Python from the command
line is either `python` (Windows) or `python3` (linux & macOS, for backward
compatibilty with Python version 2).  You will need access to a command line,
via the command window or a PowerShell window for Windows, or a terminal window
in linux & macOS.
## Creating and Activating a Python Virtual Environment
##### docs/authentication/AuthenticationMethods.md
# Authentication Methods
ScubaGoggles supports both OAuth and Service Accounts for authorization/authentication. See the following table for the tradeoffs between the two methods.
| OAuth    | Service Account |
| -------- | ------- |
| + Allows user consent to specific scopes | - Requires Domain-Wide Delegation (DWD) for the Policy API and a Delegated Admin Service Account (DASA) for read-only access to the Group Settings API. |
| - Requires a browser for authentication | + Does not require a browser for authentication, allowing for more automation. |
After determining which method is most appropriate for your organization, follow the instructions in either [Using OAuth](OAuth.md) or [Using a Service Account](ServiceAccount.md).
## Navigation
- Continue to [Using OAuth](OAuth.md)
- Continue to [Using a Service Account](ServiceAccount.md)
- Return to [Documentation Home](/README.md)
##### docs/authentication/ServiceAccount.md
# Using a Service Account
Only complete this section if not authenticating via [OAuth](OAuth.md). See [Authentication Methods](AuthenticationMethods.md) for more details.
> [!Important]
> ScubaGoggles requires the service account to have [domain-wide delegation of authority](https://support.google.com/a/answer/162106?hl=en) to function. 
1. Login to https://console.cloud.google.com and navigate to your GCP project.
1. From the hamburger menu, select **IAM & Admin** -> **Service Accounts**
1. Select **+ Create service account**. Fill out the id field and then select **Create and close**
1. Copy the email associated with your service account, for later use
1. Click on the newly created service account then click **Keys** -> **Add key** -> **Create new key** -> **JSON** -> **Create**
1. Move the credentials file to a safe location. There is no set location requirement for this file, but it should be saved somewhere it won't be inadvertently deleted or accessed by unauthorized entities.
1. Optionally run the following command to configure ScubaGoggles to use those credentials by default: `scubagoggles setup --credentials [path to JSON credentials file]`. If you skip this step, you will be required to indicate the path at run time using the `credentials` parameter (see [Parameters](/docs/usage/Parameters.md)).
1. Now login to [admin.google.com](https://admin.google.com/) and navigate to **Security** -> **Access and data control** -> **API controls**
1. Select **MANAGE DOMAIN WIDE DELEGATION**
1. Select **Add new**
1. Enter the `client_id` from the downloaded credentials (also visible after clicking on the created Service account under Details -> Unique ID)
1. Enter each Domain-wide delegation scope as listed in [Permissions](../prerequisites/Prerequisites.md#domain-wide-delegation-scopes) in the OAuth scopes field. (Tip: you can copy and paste the entire block into the field.)
1. Select **AUTHORIZE**
1. To add the Groups Reader role to your service account, navigate to **Account** -> **Admin Roles** in the Workspace Admin Console.
1. Locate and click the Groups Reader role, and then expand the **Admins** section.
1. Click on **Assign service accounts**
1. Enter the service account email address and click **ADD**.
1. Under Set Conditions, ensure that **Access to all groups** is selected and click **ASSIGN ROLE**
1. To add a custom role for licensing to your service account, navigate to **Account** -> **Admin Roles** in the Workspace Admin Console
1. Click **Create new role**
1. Enter a name such as "License Read" and select **CONTINUE**
1. Under **Admin Privileges** search for "license" and select **License Read**. Click **CONTINUE** then **CREATE ROLE**
1. Click on **Assign service accounts**
1. Enter the service account email address, click **ADD**, and click **ASSIGN ROLE**

that contain `:` on every platform, so a pack from GitHub can't carry Windows alternate data streams.

Windows alternate data streams on files already on your computer, such as the `Zone.Identifier` mark that
downloads get or the stream Microsoft Defender Endpoint DLP adds, are not part of the digest and don't stop a
pack. PowerShell never runs a stream's content, a pack's code can read one only with a call you can see when you
review it, and only someone who can already change the stored files could add one.

A module that the pack runs in a separate process from your own install (`"Install": "User"`) cannot be pinned:
it is shown as High risk, and `AllowExternalEnvironments: false` refuses the pack.

Each module a pack uses is pinned the same way, by the digest of its folder. A module you installed yourself
(used when the pack policy's `AllowExternalEnvironments` is on) is pinned by its digest at approval, raises the
pack to High risk, and needs approving again when it changes.

content.text:
Both tools can become packs, and the [Zero Trust Assessment pack](packs/zero-trust-assessment/tests/Test.ZTA.ps1) already shows how. But you're only half right about multi-language: packs don't support it yet. Below are the facts, then the prerequisites.

## Multi-language: not yet

- The pack manifest has a `Runtime` key, but [Read-MtPackManifest.ps1:93](powershell/internal/packs/Read-MtPackManifest.ps1:93) refuses anything other than `Script` (PowerShell). Its message says "packs in other languages need a newer Maester" (design section 4.8).
- What does work in any language: a pack's PowerShell test can start an outside process, and that process can report progress with `##maester[progress]` lines.
- A pack can only declare PowerShell Gallery modules. `Uses` accepts `Services`, `GraphScopes`, `TenantWrites`, `Network` and `Modules`. There's no way to say "needs Python 3.11, `scubagoggles` from PyPI and the OPA binary".

So both packs would be a PowerShell wrapper around a tool the user installs, like the ZTA pack (`Install: User`, `Process: Child`).

## What makes this easy

- **Both tools write the same results file.** It's `ScubaResults_<uuid>.json` with `MetaData` (TenantId, Tool, ToolVersion, TimestampZulu), `Summary`, `AnnotatedFailedPolicies`, `Results` and `Raw`. Results are grouped by product, and each control has `Control ID`, `Requirement`, `Result`, `Criticality` and `Details`. One mapper can serve both packs.
- **The ZTA pack does the rest already.** It runs the tool in a child process, or reads an existing report from a `ReportPath` setting. It checks the report's age and tenant ID, and embeds the tool's own HTML report as an attachment. A family test with a generated `catalog.json` gives one result row per control.
- **Licence:** both repositories are CC0, so generating catalogs from their baseline files is fine.

## ScubaGear v2.0.0 (released 2026-10-22, 172 current policies)

- **Windows PowerShell 5.1 only.** `CompatiblePSEditions = 'Desktop'`, and its docs still say Windows only. Maester needs pwsh 7.4, so the child process has to be `powershell.exe`, not the current pwsh like the ZTA pack. That makes the pack Windows-only. v2.0 dropped the EXO, SharePoint, PnP and PowerApps modules and now needs only `Microsoft.Graph.Authentication` and `powershell-yaml`. An open issue ([cisagov/ScubaGear#2211](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/issues/2211)) has a working PowerShell 7/Linux proof of concept, so this may change.
- **It needs its own process anyway.** It pins `Microsoft.Graph.Authentication` to 2.25.0 or older, which would clash with Maester's Graph module if both loaded in one process.
- **OPA binary:** `Install-ScubaDependencies` downloads OPA 1.20.2 into `~/.scubagear/Tools`.
- **Separate sign-in.** It can't reuse Maester's token, so the user signs in a second time, or the pack passes Maester's app settings (AppID, certificate thumbprint, organisation) to `Invoke-SCuBA`.
- **The results file holds raw tenant data.** `Raw` is the full settings export, so it has to go in a temporary folder that's deleted afterwards, as the ZTA pack does.
- **Result mapping:**
  - `Pass` → Passed and `Fail` → Failed.
  - `Warning` (a SHOULD control that failed) → Failed at lower severity, or Investigate.
  - `N/A` and criticalities such as `Shall/Not-Implemented` or `3rd Party` → Skipped, with the reason.
  - `Error` → Error.
  - `Requirement` contains HTML, which needs sanitising.

### Overlap with the built-in CISA suite

This is the biggest decision for ScubaGear. `tests/cisa` already has 79 native tests mapped to `cisa-scuba` (framework version "ScubaGear main, 2026-10-11"). Running the pack as well would report most `MS.AAD`, `MS.EXO` and `MS.SHAREPOINT` controls twice. Options:

1. Position the pack as "run CISA's own tool" for the products Maester doesn't cover (Teams, Power Platform, Power BI), and tell users to skip the built-in CISA suite when they turn it on.
2. Have the pack's rows carry `Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'` so the framework view merges the two.

Whichever you pick, v2.0 also affects the built-in suite: Defender is retired in favour of SecuritySuite, and `MS.AAD.3.2v2`, `MS.AAD.9.1v1`, `MS.EXO.2.2v3` (SPF soft fail now passes) and the new SharePoint 1.3/3.x policies have changed. The framework file already has 23 SECURITYSUITE entries, but it predates the release by 11 days. It needs a diff against the v2.0.0 tag either way.

## ScubaGoggles v1.1.0 (on PyPI, 138 policies)

- **Runs anywhere:** Python 3.11 or later, `pip install scubagoggles`, and OPA, which `scubagoggles setup` downloads.
- **Auth is the hard part.** Either an OAuth client from a Google Cloud project with a Super Admin sign-in, or a service account. The service account needs domain-wide delegation for 11 scopes, the Groups Reader role and a custom License Read role. Maester has no Google service, so the pack needs a connector (`<CODE>.GoogleWorkspace`) that holds the credentials path and checks it.
- **Baselines:** Gmail, Drive, Common Controls, Calendar, Chat, Meet, Groups, Sites, Classroom, Gemini and Assured Controls. No `cisa-scuba` framework covers these yet.
- **Conflicts with your plan for Google.** Your notes say the first official pack would be a native Google Workspace pack. Wrapping ScubaGoggles could replace that, or sit next to it as "the CISA baseline for GWS".

## Prerequisites, in order

1. **Decide how far "multi-language" goes in v1.**
   - Option A (smaller): add `Uses.Tools`, for example `{ "Name": "scubagoggles", "Kind": "Python", "MinimumVersion": "1.1.0", "Install": "User" }` and `{ "Name": "opa" }`, so the install prompt, the scan and the pack page show them. Treat them like an `Install: User` module: High risk, and refused when `AllowExternalEnvironments` is off.
   - Option B: build real `Runtime` kinds.
   - Either one is a design change that needs your ruling.
2. **Let a child-process test start Windows PowerShell 5.1**, including a check that skips cleanly on Linux and macOS (only needed for ScubaGear).
3. **Factor the ZTA pack's child-process runner and import mode into helpers** both packs can reuse.
4. **Rule on the CISA suite overlap**, and refresh `cisa-scuba.json` against ScubaGear v2.0.0.
5. **Decide on IDs and codes.** Two built-in packs (`maester.scubagear` and `maester.scubagoggles`) or one with two suites, and codes that don't overlap the reserved `CISA` prefix.
6. **Decide whether a pack can carry a framework file**, so GWS controls get a `cisa-scuba-gws` framework. Today framework files only exist under `tests/<suite>/frameworks/`.
7. **Add catalog generators** like `build/zta/`, one per tool, that read the CC0 baseline Markdown at a pinned release tag.

My recommendation is to start with ScubaGoggles in import mode: the user runs `scubagoggles gws` and Maester reads the results file. It works on every platform, doesn't collide with existing tests, and needs no runtime changes. Then add collect mode once option A exists. ScubaGear makes more sense after you've ruled on the CISA overlap, and ideally after its PowerShell 7 support lands.

Both repositories are cloned (shallow) in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-merill-github-maester/c01385b4-b063-4eac-9479-8c7a224a2960/scratchpad/upstream`.

function Test-MtBuiltInPackCode {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns $true when Code is the code of a pack that ships with Maester and Path is inside that pack.

    .DESCRIPTION
    A pack that ships with Maester may name a test family by its bare code (ZTA for the Zero Trust
    Assessment pack), which the test ID grammar would otherwise reject because it has no digit or separator.
    The exception holds only for a file inside that pack's folder, so a custom test cannot use the bare code.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [string] $Code,

        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [string] $Path
    )

    $full = [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath($Path)
    foreach ($pack in @(Get-MtBuiltInPack)) {
        if (-not $pack.Manifest -or -not $pack.Manifest.Code -or -not ([string]$pack.Manifest.Code).Equals($Code, [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) { continue }
        $root = [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath($pack.Root).TrimEnd('/', '\') + [System.IO.Path]::DirectorySeparatorChar
        if ($full.StartsWith($root, [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) { return $true }
    }
    $false
}
# Maintaining the Zero Trust Assessment pack

The pack is in [`packs/zero-trust-assessment`](../../packs/zero-trust-assessment).

`catalog.json` lists the assessment's tests, titles and ratings for the pack's listing. It is generated; do not
edit it. To move the pack to a new version of the module, run:

```powershell
./build/zta/Update-MtZtaCatalog.ps1 -SourcePath <ZeroTrustAssessment module folder or repository clone>
```

# CISA Google Workspace Secure Configuration Baseline for Gmail

Gmail is the Google Workspace offering for sending and receiving email. Users can upload attachments to emails and send them to a given email address. Additional Gmail features include integrating with other Google applications, such as Meet and Chat. This Secure Configuration Baseline (SCB) provides specific policies to strengthen Gmail security.

The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency's (CISA) Secure Cloud Business Applications (SCuBA) project provides guidance and capabilities to secure federal civilian executive branch (FCEB) agencies' cloud business application environments and protect federal information that is created, accessed, shared, and stored in those environments.

The CISA SCuBA SCBs for GWS help secure federal information assets stored within GWS cloud business application environments through consistent, effective, and manageable security configurations. CISA created baselines tailored to the federal government's threats and risk tolerance. Organizations outside of the federal government may also find these baselines to be useful references to help reduce risks even if such organizations have different risk tolerances or face different threats.

For non-federal users, the information in this document is being provided "as is" for INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, some controls and settings are not available in all products. CISA has no control over vendor changes to products offerings or features. Accordingly, these SCuBA SCBs for GWS may not be applicable to the products available to you. This document does not address, ensure compliance with, or supersede any law, regulation, or other authority. Entities are responsible for complying with any recordkeeping, privacy, and other laws that may apply to the use of technology. This document is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit for anyone against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.

This baseline is based on Google documentation available in the [Gmail Google Workspace Admin Help Center](https://support.google.com/a/topic/9202?hl=en&ref_topic=9197) and addresses the following:

    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [object] $PlanRow,
        [Parameter()] [AllowNull()] [psmoduleinfo] $Module,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [pscustomobject] $RunConfig,
        [Parameter()] [AllowNull()] [pscustomobject] $Selection
    )

    $test = $PlanRow.Test
    $parentRow = {
        param($disposition, $code, $detail)
        $copy = [pscustomobject]@{} ; foreach ($prop in $PlanRow.PSObject.Properties) { $copy | Add-Member -NotePropertyName $prop.Name -NotePropertyValue $prop.Value }
        $copy.Disposition = $disposition; $copy.ReasonCode = $code; $copy.ReasonDetail = $detail
        ConvertTo-MtNativeRow -PlanRow $copy
    }

    $sourceItem = [Maester.Engine.MtWorkItem]::new()
    $sourceItem.Id = $test.Id
    $sourceItem.Command = $test.InstanceSource
    $sourceItem.Title = [string]$test.Title
    $sourceItem.Module = $Module
    $sourceItem.Lane = 'Main'
    if ($PlanRow.TimeoutSeconds -gt 0) { $sourceItem.TimeoutSeconds = $PlanRow.TimeoutSeconds }
    $source = @(Invoke-MtEngineRun -WorkItem $sourceItem -Module $ExecutionContext.SessionState.Module) | Select-Object -First 1
    Write-MtTestOutput -Complete
    $empty = @{ Instances = @(); PlanRows = @{} }
    switch ([string]$source.Status) {
        'Completed' { $instances = @($source.Output | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ }) }
        'Skipped' { return [pscustomobject]($empty + @{ Rows = @(& $parentRow 'Skipped' 'TestSkipped' $source.Reason) }) }
        'Timeout' {
            return [pscustomobject]($empty + @{ Rows = @(& $parentRow 'Error' 'InstanceSourceFailed' "The instance source $($test.InstanceSource) did not finish within $($PlanRow.TimeoutSeconds) seconds.") })
        }
        default {
            return [pscustomobject]($empty + @{ Rows = @(& $parentRow 'Error' 'InstanceSourceFailed' "The instance source $($test.InstanceSource) failed: $($source.Reason)") })
        }
    }
    if ($instances.Count -eq 0) {
        return [pscustomobject]($empty + @{ Rows = @(& $parentRow 'Skipped' 'NoInstances' 'There is nothing in this tenant for this test to check.') })
    }

    $seen = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)
    foreach ($i in $instances) {
        $suffix = [string]$i.Id
        if ($suffix -notmatch '^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}\z' -or -not $seen.Add($suffix)) {
            return [pscustomobject]($empty + @{ Rows = @(& $parentRow 'Error' 'InvalidInstanceId' "The instance source returned an invalid or repeated instance ID '$suffix'.") })
        }
    }

    $run = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
    $rows = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
    $planRows = @{}
    $copyRow = {
        $copy = [pscustomobject]@{}
        foreach ($prop in $PlanRow.PSObject.Properties) { $copy | Add-Member -NotePropertyName $prop.Name -NotePropertyValue $prop.Value }

        $reason = $null
        if (@($PlanRow.InstancePatterns).Count -gt 0 -and -not (Test-MtIdMatch -Id $instanceId -Pattern $PlanRow.InstancePatterns)) {
            $reason = @('NotSelected', 'Not in the list of test IDs to run.')
        } elseif ($Selection -and (Test-MtIdMatch -Id $instanceId -Pattern $Selection.ExcludeTestId)) {
            $reason = @('ExcludedById', "Excluded by ID.")
        } else {

            if ($setting -and $setting.PSObject.Properties['Enabled'] -and $setting.Enabled -eq $false) {
                $reason = @('DisabledByConfig', $(if ($setting.PSObject.Properties['Reason'] -and $setting.Reason) { [string]$setting.Reason } else { 'Disabled in the Maester config.' }))
            }
        }
        if ($reason) {
            $copy = [pscustomobject]@{}; foreach ($prop in $PlanRow.PSObject.Properties) { $copy | Add-Member -NotePropertyName $prop.Name -NotePropertyValue $prop.Value }
            $copy.Disposition = 'NotRun'; $copy.ReasonCode = $reason[0]; $copy.ReasonDetail = $reason[1]
            $rows.Add((ConvertTo-MtNativeRow -PlanRow $copy -Instance $i))
        } else {
            $own = if ($RunConfig.TestSettingsHash -and $RunConfig.TestSettingsHash.ContainsKey($instanceId)) { $RunConfig.TestSettingsHash[$instanceId] } else { $null }
            $ownParameters = if ($own -and $own.PSObject.Properties['Parameters']) { $own.Parameters } else { $null }
            $hasTimeout = $own -and $own.PSObject.Properties['TimeoutSeconds'] -and $null -ne $own.TimeoutSeconds
            if ($null -ne $ownParameters -or $hasTimeout) {

                    $overrideValues = @{}
                    foreach ($e in @($PlanRow.EffectiveParameters)) {

                        elseif ($e.Source -eq 'Parameter') { $overrideValues[$e.Name] = $e.Value }

function Add-MtReportAttachment {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Embeds an HTML report from another tool in the Maester HTML report, opened with one click.
    .DESCRIPTION
    Call this from a test, an instance source or a pack when the tool it runs writes its own single-file
    HTML report (for example the Microsoft Zero Trust Assessment). The file is read at once, so the tool's
    output folder can be deleted afterwards.
    The HTML report shows a button for each attachment on the overview page, and on the result of the test
    that added it. The button shows the attached report inside the Maester report, beside its navigation, with an option to open it in a new browser tab. The report is stored compressed
    (gzip, then Base64), so a 10 MB report adds about 2 MB to the Maester report.
    Attachments are kept only in the HTML report and the results that Invoke-Maester -PassThru returns. The
    JSON results file lists each attachment's name and size without its content. The HTML report leaves
    attachments out when -RedactUserIdentity is used, because Maester cannot redact another tool's report.
    The attached page runs in a sandboxed frame, with its scripts in an origin of their own, so it cannot read or
    change the Maester report or its data. Adding a second attachment with the same name from the same test
    replaces the first.
    .EXAMPLE
    Add-MtReportAttachment -Name 'Zero Trust Assessment' -Path ./zt/ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html
    Embeds the Zero Trust Assessment report in the Maester report of this run.
    .EXAMPLE
    Add-MtReportAttachment -Name 'Tenant inventory' -Content $html
    Embeds an HTML page built in memory.
    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Add-MtReportAttachment
    #>
    [CmdletBinding(DefaultParameterSetName = 'Path')]
    [OutputType([void])]
    param(
        # The label of the button that opens the attachment, for example 'Zero Trust Assessment'.
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $Name,
        # Path of a single-file HTML report to embed.
        [Parameter(Mandatory, ParameterSetName = 'Path')]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $Path,
        # The HTML to embed, when it is not in a file.
        [Parameter(Mandatory, ParameterSetName = 'Content')]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $Content
    )
    if ($PSCmdlet.ParameterSetName -eq 'Path') {
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path -PathType Leaf)) {
            Write-Warning "Add-MtReportAttachment: $Path was not found, so '$Name' is not attached to the report."
            return
        }
        $bytes = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes((Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $Path).ProviderPath)

Reads the Google Workspace Secure Configuration Baselines (baselines/*.md) that ship with ScubaGoggles and writes
packs/scubagoggles/catalog.json: the ScubaGoggles version it was built from and one entry per policy, with its
requirement, criticality, indicators, rationale, NIST SP 800-53 and MITRE ATT&CK mappings and the steps to
configure it. Nothing is run.

The pack reads the catalog at run time for each result's description and remediation, which the ScubaResults
file does not hold. A policy added in a newer version of ScubaGoggles is still reported, with the text of the
results file only; rerun this script when the pack moves to a new version.

.PARAMETER SourcePath
A clone of https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles, or the installed scubagoggles package folder (the one that
holds __init__.py and baselines/). Defaults to the package of the scubagoggles command on the PATH.

.PARAMETER OutputPath
Where to write the catalog. Defaults to packs/scubagoggles/catalog.json in this repository.

.EXAMPLE
./build/scubagoggles/Update-MtScubaGogglesCatalog.ps1 -SourcePath ~/src/ScubaGoggles
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $SourcePath,

    [string] $OutputPath = (Join-Path -Path $PSScriptRoot -ChildPath '..' -AdditionalChildPath '..', 'packs', 'scubagoggles', 'catalog.json')
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

if (-not $SourcePath) {
    $python = Get-Command -Name python3, python -CommandType Application -ErrorAction Ignore | Select-Object -First 1
    if (-not $python) { throw 'Python is not on the PATH. Pass -SourcePath.' }
    $SourcePath = & $python.Source -I -c 'import os, scubagoggles; print(os.path.dirname(scubagoggles.__file__))'
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not $SourcePath) { throw 'The scubagoggles package is not installed. Install it, or pass -SourcePath.' }
}
$packageRoot = @($SourcePath, (Join-Path $SourcePath 'scubagoggles')) |
    Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $_ '__init__.py') } | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $packageRoot) { throw "No scubagoggles package (__init__.py) under $SourcePath." }
$init = Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $packageRoot '__init__.py') -Raw
if ($init -notmatch "__version__\s*=\s*'([^']+)'") { throw "No __version__ in $packageRoot/__init__.py." }
$version = $Matches[1]
$baselinesPath = Join-Path $packageRoot 'baselines'

# The text of a policy's lines, without the badge lines and the blank lines around them.
function Join-MtScubaLine {
    param([string[]] $Line)
    (@($Line | Where-Object { $_ -notmatch '^\s*\[!\[' }) -join "`n").Trim()
}

$policies = foreach ($file in Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $baselinesPath -Filter '*.md' | Where-Object Name -ne 'README.md' | Sort-Object Name) {
    $lines = @(Get-Content -LiteralPath $file.FullName -Encoding utf8)
    $product = if ($lines[0] -match 'Baseline for (.+)$') { $Matches[1].Trim() } else { $file.BaseName }
    $group = $null
    $groupNumber = $null
    $current = $null
    # The policies of the current group, and its ### Implementation section, for groups whose steps are shared.
    $groupPolicies = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
    $implementation = $null
    $own = @{}
    $section = $null

    $finishGroup = {
        foreach ($p in $groupPolicies) {
            $steps = if ($own.ContainsKey($p.ControlId)) { $own[$p.ControlId] } elseif ($implementation) { $implementation } else { $null }
            if ($steps) { $p.Remediation = (($steps -join "`n").Trim() -replace '\n{3,}', "`n`n") }
            $p
        }
        $groupPolicies.Clear()
    }

    for ($i = 0; $i -lt $lines.Count; $i++) {
        $line = $lines[$i]
        if ($line -match '^## (\d+)\.\s+(.+)$') {
            & $finishGroup
            $groupNumber = $Matches[1]; $group = $Matches[2].Trim()
            $implementation = $null; $own = @{}; $section = $null; $current = $null
            continue
        }
        if ($line -match '^## ') {
            & $finishGroup
            $group = $null; $implementation = $null; $own = @{}; $section = $null; $current = $null
            continue
        }
        if (-not $group) { continue }
        if ($line -match '^### Implementation') { $implementation = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new(); $section = $implementation; $current = $null; continue }
        if ($line -match '^### ') { $section = $null; $current = $null; continue }
        if ($line -match '^#### (GWS\.[A-Z]+\.\d+\.\d+v\d+)\s+[Ii]nstructions:?\s*$') {
            $own[$Matches[1]] = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
            $section = $own[$Matches[1]]
            continue
        }
        if ($line -match '^#### (GWS\.([A-Z]+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+))v(\d+)\s*$') {
            $controlId = $line.Substring(5).Trim()
            $requirement = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
            $j = $i + 1
            while ($j -lt $lines.Count -and $lines[$j] -notmatch '^\s*(- _|- MITRE|####|###|\[!\[)') {
                $requirement.Add($lines[$j]); $j++
            }
            $indicators = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
            while ($j -lt $lines.Count -and $lines[$j] -notmatch '^\s*- ' -and $lines[$j] -notmatch '^#') {
                if ($lines[$j] -match '^\s*\[!\[([^\]]+)\]') { $indicators.Add($Matches[1]) }
                $j++
            }
            $text = Join-MtScubaLine -Line $requirement
            $criticality = if ($text -cmatch '\bSHALL\b') { 'SHALL' } elseif ($text -cmatch '\bSHOULD\b') { 'SHOULD' } elseif ($text -cmatch '\bMAY\b') { 'MAY' } else { $null }
            $current = [ordered]@{
                Id          = 'SCUBA.GWS.{0}.{1}.{2}' -f $Matches[2], $Matches[3], $Matches[4]
                ControlId   = $controlId
                Product     = $product
                Baseline    = $file.BaseName
                Group       = $group
                GroupNumber = $groupNumber
                Title       = ($text -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
                Criticality = $criticality
                Indicators  = @($indicators | Select-Object -Unique)
                Rationale   = $null
                Note        = $null
                Nist        = @()
                Mitre       = @()
                Remediation = $null
                Url         = 'https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles/blob/v{0}/scubagoggles/baselines/{1}#{2}' -f $version, $file.Name, ($controlId.ToLowerInvariant() -replace '[^a-z0-9]', '')
            }
            $groupPolicies.Add($current)
            $section = $null
            $i = $j - 1
            continue
        }
        if ($current -and -not $section) {
            if ($line -match '^\s*- _Rationale:_\s*(.+)$') { $current.Rationale = $Matches[1].Trim() }
            elseif ($line -match '^\s*- _Note:_\s*(.+)$') { $current.Note = $Matches[1].Trim() }
            elseif ($line -match '^\s*- _NIST SP 800-53[^:]*:_\s*(.+)$') { $current.Nist = @($Matches[1] -split ',\s*' | ForEach-Object { $_.Trim() } | Where-Object { $_ }) }
            elseif ($line -match 'attack\.mitre\.org/techniques/(T\d{4})(?:/(\d{3}))?') {
                $technique = if ($Matches[2]) { "$($Matches[1]).$($Matches[2])" } else { $Matches[1] }
                $current.Mitre = @($current.Mitre) + $technique | Select-Object -Unique
            }
        }
        if ($null -ne $section) { $section.Add($line) }
    }
    & $finishGroup
}

$ids = @($policies | Group-Object -Property { $_.Id } | Where-Object Count -gt 1)
if ($ids) { throw "The baselines give more than one policy the ID $($ids.Name -join ', ')." }

$catalog = [ordered]@{
    '$comment' = 'Generated by build/scubagoggles/Update-MtScubaGogglesCatalog.ps1 from the ScubaGoggles baselines (CC0 1.0, CISA). Do not edit by hand.'
    Tool       = 'ScubaGoggles'
    Version    = $version
    Source     = 'https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles'
    Policies   = @($policies | Sort-Object { $_.Baseline }, { [int]$_.GroupNumber }, { [int]($_.ControlId -split '\.')[3].Split('v')[0] })
}
$catalog | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $OutputPath -Encoding utf8NoBOM
Write-Information -InformationAction Continue -MessageData "Wrote $(@($policies).Count) policies from ScubaGoggles $version to $OutputPath."
