---
title: Zero Trust Assessment pack
sidebar_position: 4
description: Run Microsoft's Zero Trust Assessment from Maester and see each of its results in the Maester report.
---

# Zero Trust Assessment pack

This pack runs Microsoft's [Zero Trust Assessment](https://aka.ms/zerotrust/assessment) and shows each of its
results in the Maester report, next to Maester's own checks. It ships with Maester and does not run unless you
ask for it.

Each assessment result is one row, `ZTA.<assessment test ID>` (for example `ZTA.21770`), with the
assessment's title, risk level (as the severity), description, remediation steps and findings. Results are tagged
`ZeroTrust` and `ZeroTrust.<pillar>` (`ZeroTrust.Identity`, `ZeroTrust.Devices` and so on).

The pack's ID is `maester.zero-trust-assessment`. It needs no `Install-MtPack`: it is part of the Maester module,
and `Get-MtPack` lists it.

## Run it

Install the assessment's module once, connect Maester to the tenant, then name the pack:

```powershell
Install-Module ZeroTrustAssessment -Scope CurrentUser
Connect-Maester
Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA -SkipBuiltIn    # only the Zero Trust Assessment
Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA                 # Maester's tests and the assessment
```

You don't run `Connect-ZtAssessment` yourself. The assessment runs in a separate PowerShell process, which can't
use the sign-ins of your session, so Maester signs in there for you (see
[Let Maester run the assessment](#let-maester-run-the-assessment)). After an interactive `Connect-Maester` you
sign in a second time, in the browser, for the assessment. `Connect-Maester` is still needed: it tells the
assessment which tenant to sign in to, and the pack is skipped while Maester is not connected to Graph. If you
read a report you already have (below), you run `Connect-ZtAssessment` and `Invoke-ZtAssessment` yourself first.

The pack is a long-running test, so `Invoke-Maester` leaves it out unless you name it. These also run it:

```powershell
Invoke-Maester -TestId ZTA          # only the Zero Trust Assessment
Invoke-Maester -Suite ZTA              # the same
Invoke-Maester -IncludeLongRunning          # everything, including the assessment
```

The pack itself stays enabled, so naming it is enough; it is the long-running flag that keeps it out of a plain
`Invoke-Maester`. To remove it entirely, set `Packs: [{ "Id": "maester.zero-trust-assessment", "Enabled": false }]`.

To run it on every run, add it to `Selection.TestId` in `maester-config.json`, or set
`Selection.IncludeLongRunning` to `true`. Give it time with `Execution.LongRunningTimeoutSeconds`: the assessment
can take an hour or more on a large tenant.

The pack gets the assessment's results one of two ways.

### Read a report you already have (recommended in CI)

Run the assessment as its own step, then point Maester at the report it wrote:

```powershell
Install-Module ZeroTrustAssessment -Scope CurrentUser
Connect-ZtAssessment
Invoke-ZtAssessment -Path ./zt -NoBrowser
```

```json
{ "GlobalSettings": { "ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath": "./zt" } }
```

Then, in a new PowerShell session (the assessment's modules can't share one with Maester's), connect Maester to
the same tenant and run the pack:

```powershell
Connect-Maester
Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA
```

`ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath` takes the report file (`ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.json`), the folder given to
`Invoke-ZtAssessment -Path`, or its `zt-export` folder. Maester refuses a report written for another tenant than the
one it is connected to, and one older than `ZeroTrustAssessment.MaxReportAgeDays` (7 by default; 0 turns the check
off).

### Let Maester run the assessment

Without `ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath`, Maester runs the assessment itself. Install the module first:

```powershell
Install-Module ZeroTrustAssessment -Scope CurrentUser
```

The assessment loads its own versions of the Microsoft Graph, Exchange Online and Az modules, which cannot share
a PowerShell session with the ones Maester has loaded. So Maester starts it in a separate `pwsh` process, which
signs in with `Connect-ZtAssessment`:

- It signs in to the tenant Maester is connected to.
- When Maester is connected to Graph app-only with a certificate, it uses the same app and certificate. The app
  needs the Graph application permissions that `Get-ZtGraphScope` lists.
- When Maester is connected app-only another way (a client secret, a managed identity or workload identity
  federation), the pack is skipped with the reason: the assessment signs in app-only only with a certificate. See
  [Run it in a pipeline](#run-it-in-a-pipeline).
- Otherwise it signs in interactively, so you sign in a second time. Without a browser, for example over SSH, set
  `ZeroTrustAssessment.Connect` to `{ "UseDeviceCode": true }`.

While it runs, what the assessment writes is shown live: in the full-screen dashboard of an interactive run it
scrolls in a box in the middle of the screen, under the phases of the run, and in other modes (CI, redirected
output, `-Verbosity Normal`) it is written to the console, indented. The assessment runs with `-ShowLog`, so it lists
the tests it runs, and its progress bars become one line at the bottom of the box that updates in place. Set
`ZeroTrustAssessment.ShowLog` to `false` for its shorter output.

The top of the box shows where the assessment is, read once a second from the progress the assessment keeps for
its own progress page and from the progress logs it writes in its output folder:

- the six stages of the assessment as a track (Export, Tests, Tenant info, Results, Report data, HTML report),
  with the step of the stage it is on, such as "Importing Data into Database";
- a bar of the exports or tests done of how many, the percentage, how many failed and are running, and the time
  left;
- each export or test that is running, with what it is doing and how long it has run, and the ones that finished,
  with their result and how long they took, listed the way the dashboard lists Maester's own tests (tests by
  their `ZTA.` ID and title);
- each export, database import or test that fails or times out, with its error. The box counts them.

The rest of the dashboard follows the assessment while it runs:

- the Results panel and the result blocks over the box count the assessment's results (passed, failed,
  investigate, skipped) as its tests finish;
- the assessment's pillars are listed where Maester's products usually are, each with a bar and its counts;
- the Pace graph next to the logo draws how long each export and test took, and the Slowest panel lists the
  slowest of them.

Outside the dashboard the stage is written when it changes, each export and test as it finishes with its result
and time, the counts at most every ten seconds, and each failure as it happens. This needs version 3.1 or later of the ZeroTrustAssessment module; with an earlier version the
box shows the log only.

The assessment's own report and raw export go to a temporary folder that Maester deletes after reading it, because
the export holds tenant data. Set `ZeroTrustAssessment.OutputPath` to keep them.

## Run it in a pipeline

In GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps or any other pipeline, nobody is there to sign in, so the assessment signs in
as a service principal. `Connect-ZtAssessment` signs in app-only only with a certificate, found by thumbprint in
the certificate store of the computer it runs on. A client secret, a managed identity or workload identity
federation (the OIDC sign-in in [Maester's GitHub guide](../monitoring/github.md)) is enough for Maester's own
tests but not for the assessment.

So the pipeline needs:

1. An app registration with a certificate. Give the app the Graph application permissions that
   `Get-ZtGraphScope` lists (run it after `Import-Module ZeroTrustAssessment`), plus Maester's own permissions if
   the same run includes Maester's tests. The assessment's Azure, Exchange Online, Security & Compliance and
   SharePoint tests need the app to have the roles the
   [Zero Trust Assessment documentation](https://aka.ms/zerotrust/assessment) lists for app-only sign-in; to
   leave those services out, set `ZeroTrustAssessment.Connect` to `{ "Service": ["Graph"] }`.
2. The certificate as a PFX file, saved base64-encoded in a pipeline secret with its password.
3. A step that adds the certificate to the current user's certificate store, connects Maester to Graph with it
   by thumbprint, and runs the pack. The child process finds the same certificate by its thumbprint.

A GitHub Actions workflow that does this on a schedule, with the secrets `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`,
`ZTA_CERTIFICATE` (the base64 PFX) and `ZTA_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`:

```yaml
name: Zero Trust Assessment
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 3 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  zero-trust:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 360
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Run the Zero Trust Assessment with Maester
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          TENANT_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          CERTIFICATE: ${{ secrets.ZTA_CERTIFICATE }}
          CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ZTA_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          Install-Module Maester, ZeroTrustAssessment -Scope CurrentUser -Force

          # Add the certificate to the current user's store, where the assessment looks for it.
          $flags = 'PersistKeySet, Exportable'
          $cert = [System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.X509Certificate2]::new(
              [Convert]::FromBase64String($env:CERTIFICATE), $env:CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD, $flags)
          $store = [System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.X509Store]::new('My', 'CurrentUser')
          $store.Open('ReadWrite'); $store.Add($cert); $store.Close()

          Connect-MgGraph -ClientId $env:CLIENT_ID -TenantId $env:TENANT_ID -CertificateThumbprint $cert.Thumbprint -NoWelcome
          Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA -NonInteractive -OutputFolder ./test-results

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: maester-zero-trust
          path: test-results
```

The assessment can take an hour or more on a large tenant: keep the job's `timeout-minutes` above that, and raise
`Execution.LongRunningTimeoutSeconds` in `maester-config.json` if Maester stops it first. On Windows runners the
same steps work in `pwsh`.

If the assessment runs somewhere else, or you'd rather keep the certificate out of the Maester step, run
`Connect-ZtAssessment -ClientId <app> -TenantId <tenant> -Certificate <thumbprint>` and
`Invoke-ZtAssessment -Path ./zt -NoBrowser` as their own step, then let Maester read the report with
`ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath` (see [Read a report you already have](#read-a-report-you-already-have-recommended-in-ci)).
Maester's step can then connect any way it likes, including OIDC, as long as it is the same tenant.

## The assessment's own report

The Maester report embeds the HTML report the assessment wrote, with its pillar dashboards and charts. Open it
with the **Zero Trust Assessment** button on the report's overview, under **Reports** in the left menu, or on any
ZTA result. It opens inside the Maester report, with an option to open it in a new browser tab, and works
offline, so the Maester report stays a single file to share.

The embedded report is compressed: a 10 MB assessment report adds about 2 MB to the Maester report. It is left
out when `ZeroTrustAssessment.EmbedReport` is `false`, when you read a report file that has no
`ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html` beside it or one folder up, and when `Invoke-Maester -RedactUserIdentity` is
used, because Maester cannot redact the assessment's report.

## Settings

All settings go in `GlobalSettings` of `maester-config.json`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath` | empty | Read this report instead of running the assessment. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.MaxReportAgeDays` | `7` | Refuse a report older than this. `0` turns the check off. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.EmbedReport` | `true` | Embed the assessment's own HTML report in the Maester report. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.OutputPath` | temporary | Where the assessment writes its report and export. Kept when set. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.Pillar` | `All` | Run one pillar only: `Identity`, `Devices`, `Network`, `Data`, `Infrastructure`, `SecOps` or `AI`. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.Tests` | all | Run only these assessment test IDs, for example `["21770", "21771"]`. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.Days` | `30` | Days of sign-in logs the assessment reads (1 to 30). |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.ShowLog` | `true` | Run the assessment with `-ShowLog`, which lists the tests it runs in its live output. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.DisableTelemetry` | `true` | The assessment sends the tenant ID to Microsoft unless this is `true`. |
| `ZeroTrustAssessment.Connect` | none | Further `Connect-ZtAssessment` parameters, for example `{ "Service": ["Graph", "Azure"], "UseDeviceCode": true }`. |

`EmergencyAccessAccounts` is passed to the assessment as well, so its Conditional Access tests leave out the same
break-glass accounts as Maester's.

## How results map

| Assessment status | Maester result |
| --- | --- |
| Passed | Passed |
| Failed | Failed |
| Investigate | Investigate |
| Skipped | Skipped, with the assessment's reason |
| Error | Error |
| Planned | Not shown: the assessment has not built the test yet |

A test that writes several rows under one ID (the Defender for Cloud recommendations) gets one row each, with a
suffix made from the row's title so that it keeps its ID from run to run.

---
title: ScubaGoggles pack
sidebar_position: 5
description: See each result of CISA's ScubaGoggles assessment of Google Workspace in the Maester report.
---

# ScubaGoggles pack

[ScubaGoggles](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles) is CISA's free tool that checks a Google Workspace tenant
against the Secure Cloud Business Applications (SCuBA) baselines for Google Workspace: Gmail, Drive and Docs,
Common Controls, Calendar, Chat, Meet, Groups, Sites, Classroom, Gemini and Assured Controls. This pack reads the
results ScubaGoggles wrote and shows each of them in the Maester report, next to Maester's own checks. It ships
with Maester and does not run unless you ask for it.

Each policy is one row, `SCUBA.GWS.<product>.<group>.<policy>`: `GWS.GMAIL.1.1v1` is `SCUBA.GWS.GMAIL.1.1`. The ID
leaves out the policy's version, so a row keeps its ID when CISA updates the policy. Each row has the policy's
requirement as its title, the baseline's rationale, the steps to configure it, its NIST SP 800-53 and MITRE
ATT&CK mappings, and what ScubaGoggles found. Rows are tagged `ScubaGoggles` and `GWS.<product>` (`GWS.GMAIL`,
`GWS.DRIVEDOCS` and so on), and policies that BOD 25-01 requires are tagged `BOD-25-01`.

The pack's ID is `maester.scubagoggles`. It needs no `Install-MtPack`: it is part of the Maester module, and
`Get-MtPack` lists it.

## Run it

ScubaGoggles is a Python tool that signs in to Google itself, so you run it first and Maester reads what it
wrote. Install it once, with Python 3.11 or later:

```bash
pip install scubagoggles
scubagoggles setup
```

`scubagoggles setup` downloads [Open Policy Agent](https://www.openpolicyagent.org/), which ScubaGoggles uses to
evaluate the policies, and asks for the output folder and the credentials file. ScubaGoggles signs in with a Google
OAuth client and a super admin, or with a service account that has domain-wide delegation; its
[authentication guide](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles/blob/main/docs/authentication/AuthenticationMethods.md)
says how to set up either one.

Then run the assessment, and point Maester at its output folder:

```bash
scubagoggles gws -o ./scubagoggles
```

```json
{ "GlobalSettings": { "ScubaGoggles.ReportPath": "./scubagoggles" } }
```

```powershell
Invoke-Maester -Pack SCUBA.GWS -SkipBuiltIn    # only the ScubaGoggles results
Invoke-Maester -Pack SCUBA.GWS                 # Maester's tests and the ScubaGoggles results
```

`ScubaGoggles.ReportPath` takes the `ScubaResults_<uuid>.json` file, the `GWSBaselineConformance_<time>` folder
that one run wrote it in, or the output folder, where Maester reads the newest run. Maester refuses a report older
than `ScubaGoggles.MaxReportAgeDays` (7 by default; 0 turns the check off), and a results file that another SCuBA
tool, such as ScubaGear, wrote.

The pack is off by default. Naming it with `-Pack` runs it; to run it on every run, turn it on in
`maester-config.json`:

```json
{ "Packs": [{ "Id": "maester.scubagoggles", "Enabled": true }] }
```

Maester does not connect to Google for this pack, so `Connect-Maester` is only needed for the other tests you run
with it.

## Run it in a pipeline

Run ScubaGoggles with a service account as its own step, then Maester in the same job:

```yaml
- name: Run ScubaGoggles
  run: |
    pip install scubagoggles
    scubagoggles setup --nodownload --opapath ~/.scubagoggles --credentials ./service-account.json --outputpath ./scubagoggles
    scubagoggles getopa -v
    scubagoggles gws --subjectemail admin@example.org --quiet

- name: Run Maester
  shell: pwsh
  run: |
    Install-Module Maester -Scope CurrentUser -Force
    Invoke-Maester -Pack SCUBA.GWS -SkipBuiltIn -NonInteractive -OutputFolder ./test-results
```

Keep the service account key in a pipeline secret, and write it to `service-account.json` in an earlier step. See
the ScubaGoggles [parameters](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles/blob/main/docs/usage/Parameters.md) for
`--subjectemail` and the other options.

## Settings

All settings go in `GlobalSettings` of `maester-config.json`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ScubaGoggles.ReportPath` | empty | The ScubaResults file, the folder one run wrote it in, or the output folder (the newest run is read). |
| `ScubaGoggles.MaxReportAgeDays` | `7` | Refuse a report older than this. `0` turns the check off. |

## How results map

| ScubaGoggles result | Maester result |
| --- | --- |
| Pass | Passed |
| Fail (a SHALL policy) | Failed, High severity |
| Warning (a SHOULD or MAY policy) | Failed, Medium or Low severity |
| No events found | Investigate: a log-based check found no event that shows the setting |
| N/A | Skipped: ScubaGoggles doesn't check the policy, so check it by hand |
| Omitted | Skipped, with the reason from your ScubaGoggles config |
| Incorrect result | Skipped, with what ScubaGoggles reported |
| Error | Error |

The severity follows the policy's criticality whatever the result: SHALL is High, SHOULD is Medium, MAY is Low.

## ScubaGoggles' own report

ScubaGoggles writes its own HTML report, `BaselineReports.html`, beside the results file. It is several files, so
the Maester report links to the baselines rather than embedding it; open it from the ScubaGoggles output folder.

## Report an issue with a policy

CISA writes and maintains the baselines and ScubaGoggles' checks. If a result, the text of a policy or its steps
look wrong, raise it in [cisagov/ScubaGoggles](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles/issues). Problems with
reading the results in Maester go to [maester365/maester](https://github.com/maester365/maester/issues).

## Licence

ScubaGoggles and the SCuBA baselines are published by CISA under
[CC0 1.0](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles/blob/main/LICENSE). This pack does not include ScubaGoggles'
code: it reads the results file it wrote. The pack's catalog of policies is generated from the baselines.

# CISA ScubaGoggles pack

[ScubaGoggles](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles) is CISA's free tool that checks a Google Workspace tenant
against the Secure Cloud Business Applications (SCuBA) baselines for Google Workspace.

This pack reads the results ScubaGoggles wrote and shows each of them in the Maester report, next to Maester's own
checks. It ships with Maester and is off until you ask for it.

Each policy is one row, `SCUBA.GWS.<product>.<group>.<policy>` (for example `SCUBA.GWS.GMAIL.1.1` for
`GWS.GMAIL.1.1v1`), with the policy's requirement, rationale, the steps to configure it and what ScubaGoggles
found. A SHALL policy that fails is High severity, a SHOULD policy Medium.

## Run it

```bash
pip install scubagoggles
scubagoggles setup
scubagoggles gws -o ./scubagoggles
```

```json
{ "GlobalSettings": { "ScubaGoggles.ReportPath": "./scubagoggles" } }
```

```powershell
Invoke-Maester -Pack SCUBA.GWS -SkipBuiltIn
```

See [maester.dev/docs/packs/scubagoggles](https://maester.dev/docs/packs/scubagoggles) for the settings, how
results map and how to run it in a pipeline.

## Report an issue with a policy

CISA writes and maintains the baselines and the checks. If a result or a policy's text looks wrong, raise it in
[cisagov/ScubaGoggles](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles/issues). Problems with reading the results in
Maester go to [maester365/maester](https://github.com/maester365/maester/issues).

# Maintaining the ScubaGoggles pack

The pack is in [`packs/scubagoggles`](../../packs/scubagoggles).

`catalog.json` lists the policies of CISA's Google Workspace baselines, with their text, mappings and steps, for
the pack's listing and for each result's description. It is generated; do not edit it. To move the pack to a new
version of ScubaGoggles, clone that release and run:

```powershell
git clone --depth 1 --branch v1.1.0 https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles ~/src/ScubaGoggles
./build/scubagoggles/Update-MtScubaGogglesCatalog.ps1 -SourcePath ~/src/ScubaGoggles
```

The script reads the baseline Markdown (`scubagoggles/baselines/*.md`), so a change to how CISA writes those files
can drop a field. After running it, check that every policy still has a title, criticality, rationale and
remediation: `./powershell/tests/functions/ScubaGogglesPack.Tests.ps1` fails when one does not.

The pack reads the ScubaResults JSON, whose shape CISA documents in
[tooloutputschema.md](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles/blob/main/docs/misc/tooloutputschema.md). When the
results ScubaGoggles writes change (a new `Result` value, say), update `Test-MtScubaGoggles` in
`packs/scubagoggles/tests/Test.SCUBA.GWS.ps1` and the fixture in `powershell/tests/fixtures/scubagoggles`.

content.text:
I've built the ScubaGoggles pack. It reads the results file that `scubagoggles gws` writes and shows each of the 138 Google Workspace policies as a row in the Maester report. Everything is on a new branch, `feat/scubagoggles-pack`, cut from `origin/main`, and nothing is committed yet.

**Tests:** run against CISA's own sample report, the pack gave 138 rows: 72 passed, 46 failed, 3 investigate and 17 skipped. An end-to-end `Invoke-Maester -Pack SCUBA.GWS` run wrote the HTML report, and a plain run leaves the pack out. Its 23 unit tests pass. The full suite (4,201 tests) had two failures:
- The generated test-builder data was out of date after I added the `SCUBA.` prefix. I regenerated it and that test now passes.
- `ZeroTrustAssessmentPack.Tests.ps1` "skips the family when the module is not installed" fails. It fails the same way on a clean `origin/main`, so my change didn't cause it.

I haven't run real ScubaGoggles against a tenant, and I haven't tried the pipeline YAML in the docs. I checked its flags against ScubaGoggles' source, but it's untested.

**Choices I made that you may want to change:**
- **Code `SCUBA.GWS`.** Test IDs are `SCUBA.GWS.GMAIL.1.1` for `GWS.GMAIL.1.1v1`. The policy's version is dropped so a row keeps its ID when CISA updates the policy, the same way the CISA suite does it. The `SCUBA.` prefix is now reserved, which leaves room for `SCUBA.M365` when ScubaGear follows.
- **Import only.** Maester never runs Python itself. If `ScubaGoggles.ReportPath` isn't set, the pack is skipped with a message that says how to fix it. The path can be the results file, the run's folder, or the output folder (the newest run wins). Reports older than 7 days are refused.
- **Off by default.** Naming it with `-Pack` runs it.
- **Result mapping:** Pass → Passed; Fail and Warning → Failed; No events found → Investigate; N/A, Omitted and Incorrect result → Skipped with the reason; Error → Error.
- **Severity follows the policy:** SHALL is High, SHOULD is Medium, MAY is Low.
- **Richer rows.** Each row gets CISA's rationale, the steps to fix it and its NIST and MITRE mappings, from a catalog generated from the CC0 baselines. Its tags are `ScubaGoggles`, `GWS.<product>`, and `BOD-25-01` where that directive requires the policy.

**Two gaps:**
- **ScubaGoggles' own HTML report isn't embedded.** It's several files and the attachment feature takes one.
- **A pack-only run needs `-SkipGraphConnect`.** Otherwise `Invoke-Maester` stops because it isn't connected to Microsoft Graph. The docs say to add the flag, and I've put up a card to fix this in Maester itself.

content.text:
`Info` is a severity, and `Warning` isn't a Maester result at all.

- **Result** (what happened) can only be one of: Passed, Failed, Investigate, Skipped, Error or NotRun.
- **Severity** (how much it matters) can be Critical, High, Medium, Low or Info.

The only `Warning` in the engine is a console message level, for things like "this path doesn't exist".

ScubaGoggles' own "Warning" isn't an "unsure". It means a SHOULD policy was checked and isn't met; a SHALL policy that isn't met is a "Fail". In Maester that's a failed check with a lower severity, so the pack maps it to:

- Fail → Failed, High severity
- Warning → Failed, Medium severity

The other two options fit worse:
- **Investigate** means "the check ran but a person has to decide". That's how I mapped "No events found", where ScubaGoggles truly can't tell. Using it for Warning would bury 16 real findings in the sample among those three unknowns.
- **Info severity** would make an unmet SHOULD look like a footnote. Maester's own CISA suite fails SHOULD policies too.

If you'd rather SHOULD failures stand out less, I'd lower them to Low severity rather than Info. MAY would be the natural Info case, but the current GWS baselines have no MAY policies: 89 are SHALL and 49 are SHOULD.

content.text:
We don't have a separate repository for the ZTA pack; it's in this repo at [packs/zero-trust-assessment](packs/zero-trust-assessment). Its design note says you ruled on 2026-10-19 that it ships with Maester and is opt-in. I checked the two local folders that look like it:
- `~/github/maester-packs` is another clone of Maester itself (its remote is blindzero's fork).
- `~/github/zerotrustassessment` is Microsoft's tool, not a pack.
- The only pack repository under maester365 on GitHub is `maester-pack-demo`.

That's why I followed the ZTA pattern. For ScubaGoggles, though, I think its own repository fits better.

**Reasons for its own repository**
- **It isn't Microsoft 365.** ZTA checks Microsoft's own tenant, so it belongs in the module. Google Workspace checks inside the Maester module stretch what Maester is.
- **It releases on CISA's schedule.** A new ScubaGoggles release would need only a new pack release, not a Maester release.
- **It tests the marketplace path.** It would go through the same install, lock file, cooldown and packs.maester.cloud listing as everyone else's packs. Your notes already planned a Google Workspace pack as the first official one on the index, and this could be it.

**What moving it changes**
- **IDs get the `MP.` prefix**, because installed packs carry it: `MP.SCUBA.GWS.GMAIL.1.1`. I'd also undo the `SCUBA.` reserved prefix and the regenerated test-builder data in this repo.
- **Users run `Install-MtPack maester365/<repo>` first**, and approve it once.
- **The unit tests move to the pack's own CI**, with `Test-MtPack` and its fixture. The catalog generator moves with it.
- **Name:** something like `maester365/maester-pack-scubagoggles`, which I'd need you to create, or `gh repo create` with your go-ahead.

**Reasons to keep it built-in:** no install or approval step, short IDs, and it's tested on every Maester change.

My recommendation is its own repository. A ScubaGear pack later would be Microsoft 365 and overlap the built-in CISA suite, so that one has a stronger case for living here.

#
# It runs only when the repository variable PACK_RELEASES is true, with release.yml. Without it the pack has no
# releases and Install-MtPack installs the default branch. See "Versions and releases" in README.md.
name: Bump version

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, reopened, synchronize, labeled, unlabeled, ready_for_review]

concurrency:
  group: bump-version-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}

jobs:
  bump:
    if: >-
      vars.PACK_RELEASES == 'true' &&
      github.event.pull_request.base.ref == 'main' &&
      github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
      !github.event.pull_request.draft
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      sha: ${{ steps.bump.outputs.sha }}
      version: ${{ steps.bump.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Raise the version
        id: bump
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
        run: |
          # Read the labels now, not from the event, so the latest label counts.
          $labels = @(gh pr view $env:PR_NUMBER --json labels --jq '.labels[].name')
          if ($labels -contains 'release:none') {
            Write-Output 'The pull request has release:none: the version stays as it is.'
            return
          }
          $part = if ($labels -contains 'release:major') { 'major' } elseif ($labels -contains 'release:minor') { 'minor' } else { 'patch' }

          git fetch --quiet origin main
          $base = [version](git show origin/main:maester-pack.json | ConvertFrom-Json).Version
          $text = Get-Content -LiteralPath maester-pack.json -Raw
          $current = [version]($text | ConvertFrom-Json).Version
          $next = switch ($part) {
            'major' { '{0}.0.0' -f ($base.Major + 1) }
            'minor' { '{0}.{1}.0' -f $base.Major, ($base.Minor + 1) }
            default { '{0}.{1}.{2}' -f $base.Major, $base.Minor, ([math]::Max($base.Build, 0) + 1) }
          }
          if ($current -eq [version]$next) {
            Write-Output "The version is already $next ($part above $base on main)."
            return
          }

          # Change only the value of the manifest's own Version, so the rest of the file keeps its layout.
          $text = ([regex]'("Version"\s*:\s*")[^"]*(")').Replace($text, "`${1}$next`${2}", 1)
          if (($text | ConvertFrom-Json).Version -ne $next) { throw 'Could not change Version in maester-pack.json.' }
          [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText((Resolve-Path maester-pack.json), $text)

          # The changelog: "## Unreleased" becomes the version. A heading this workflow wrote before (the label
          # changed, or main moved on) moves to the new version. Without either, the pull request's title is the entry.

# Checks the pack on every push and pull request: the manifest and the content checks that Install-MtPack runs
# (Test-MtPack), then every test once from this folder (Invoke-MtTest -Path). Results such as Failed are
# expected; a test the engine cannot run (bad metadata, a wrong return value, a bad parameter) fails the job.
name: Check pack

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:
  # bump-version.yml calls it on the commit that raises the version, which no push event checks.
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ref:
        description: The commit to check.
        type: string
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.ref }}

      - name: Install Maester
        shell: pwsh
        run: Install-PSResource -Name Maester -Prerelease -TrustRepository -Quiet

      - name: Check the pack
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          Import-Module Maester
          if (-not (Get-Command Test-MtPack -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
            Write-Output '::warning::This Maester version has no packs yet; the pack was not checked.'
            return
          }
          $manifest = Get-Content ./maester-pack.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
          # The maester and maester365 publishers are reserved for packs of the maester365 organisation.
          $official = $manifest.Publisher -in 'maester', 'maester365'
          $check = Test-MtPack . -Official:$official
          $check | Format-List Id, Version, IsValid, Risk, Errors, Warnings, Findings
          if (-not $check.IsValid) { throw 'The pack is not valid.' }
          if ($check.Risk -eq 'High') { throw 'The content checks rate the pack High risk.' }

      - name: Run the tests
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          Import-Module Maester
          if (-not (Get-Command Test-MtPack -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { return }
          $manifest = Get-Content ./maester-pack.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
          if ($manifest.Publisher -in 'maester', 'maester365') {
            Write-Output '::notice::Invoke-MtTest -Path does not run packs of the reserved maester365 publisher; skipped.'
            return
          }
          $results = @(Invoke-MtTest -Path .)
          $results | Format-Table Id, Result, ReasonCode -AutoSize | Out-String -Width 200
          $broken = @($results | Where-Object ReasonCode -In 'InvalidMetadata', 'InvalidReturn', 'InvalidConfiguration', 'InvalidInstanceId', 'InstanceSourceFailed')
          if ($broken) { throw "The engine could not run $($broken.Count) test(s): $($broken.Id -join ', ')" }
# Publishes a release for the version on main. After each push to main (a merged pull request), it reads Version
# from maester-pack.json and, when there is no release v<Version> yet, tags that commit v<Version> and publishes a
# release with the version's section of CHANGELOG.md as its notes. Install-MtPack installs the newest published
# release once it is older than the install cooldown. A merge with release:none keeps the version, so it
# publishes nothing. Run it by hand (workflow_dispatch) to publish the version on main if a run was missed.
#
# It runs only when the repository variable PACK_RELEASES is true, with bump-version.yml. Without it the pack has
# no releases and Install-MtPack installs the default branch. See "Versions and releases" in README.md.
name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: release

jobs:
  release:
    if: vars.PACK_RELEASES == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Publish the release
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          $version = [string](Get-Content -LiteralPath maester-pack.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).Version
          if ($version -notmatch '^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$') { throw "Version '$version' in maester-pack.json is not major.minor.patch." }
          $tag = "v$version"

          gh release view $tag --json tagName 2>$null | Out-Null

Run `scubagoggles gws`, set the `ScubaGoggles.ReportPath` setting to the results it wrote, then run
results it wrote, then run `Invoke-Maester -Pack SCUBA.GWS`.

## Versions and releases

`Install-MtPack <owner>/<repository>` installs the newest GitHub release of a pack. A repository with no release
installs its default branch instead. A copy of this repository has two ways to ship new versions:

- **Track the default branch (the default).** Push to `main` and that is what people install and update to. Nothing
  to set up; raise `Version` in `maester-pack.json` yourself when you want people to see a new number.
- **Publish releases.** Each merged pull request gets the next version and a release, so people install a fixed
  version and see what changed. Once a repository has one release, installs follow releases and ignore `main`.

To publish releases, as an admin of the repository:

1. Turn on the two workflows that do it (they do nothing until this variable is set):

   ```bash
   gh variable set PACK_RELEASES --body true -R <owner>/<repository>
   ```

2. Protect `main`, so every change comes through a pull request that is up to date, has its conversations
   resolved, passes the pack check and is squash-merged (force pushes and deleting `main` are blocked):

   ```bash
   gh api repos/<owner>/<repository>/contents/.github/rulesets/main.json -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw" |
     gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repository>/rulesets --input -
   ```

   No approval is required, so a maintainer can merge their own pull request; raise
   `required_approving_review_count` in [.github/rulesets/main.json](.github/rulesets/main.json) when the
   repository has more than one maintainer.

3. Optionally create the labels `release:major`, `release:minor`, `release:patch` and `release:none`.

Then every pull request carries the next version. [bump-version.yml](.github/workflows/bump-version.yml) sets
`Version` in `maester-pack.json` one step above the version on `main` and turns `## Unreleased` in
[CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) into that version, and pushes that commit to the pull request (pull before you push
to it again). The label picks the part to raise: `release:major`, `release:minor`, `release:patch` (the default,
also when there is no label) or `release:none`; changing the label changes the version. Write what changed under
`## Unreleased` as part of the pull request. A pull request from a fork gets no version commit: its author (or
the maintainer, before merging) raises `Version` and the changelog heading by hand.

Merging publishes the release. [release.yml](.github/workflows/release.yml) runs on each push to `main`, and when
there is no release for the version in `maester-pack.json` yet, it tags the commit `v<Version>` and publishes a
release with that version's changelog section as its notes. A pull request labelled `release:none` keeps the
version, so its merge publishes nothing once that version has a release. To publish the version already on `main`, run the Release workflow by
hand from the Actions tab. `Install-MtPack` offers a new release once it is older than the install cooldown.

This repository tracks its default branch: `PACK_RELEASES` is not set, so the two workflows do nothing here and
`Install-MtPack maester365/maester-pack-demo` installs `main`. `Version` in `maester-pack.json` is raised by hand.

## Files

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `maester-pack.json` | The manifest: ID, code, version, the suite, helpers, the connector and what the pack uses |
| `tests/` | The suite: `suite.json`, and one `Test.<ID>.ps1` and `Test.<ID>.md` per test |
| `helpers/` | Functions the tests call: the connector's settings, and the data and HTML of the report |
| `connector/` | `Connect-`, `Test-` and `Disconnect-DemoSample` for the made-up service |
| `assets/banner.png` | The image the pack index shows when it features the pack |
| `assets/insights-report.html` | The page of MP.DEMO.1008's report, with sample data so you can open it in a browser |
| `assets/chart.js/` | Chart.js 4.5.1 and its MIT licence, put inline in the report |
| `docs/report-ideas.md` | An optional guide: what a pack's report can show, and which chart library to use. A pack does not need a report |
| `tools/` | `Initialize-MtPackFromDemo`, which turns a copy into your own pack; delete the folder afterwards. The pack never loads it |

# CISA ScubaGoggles pack for Maester

A [Maester Pack](https://maester.dev/docs/next/packs) that shows the results of
[ScubaGoggles](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles) in the Maester report. ScubaGoggles is CISA's free tool
that checks a Google Workspace tenant against the Secure Cloud Business Applications (SCuBA) baselines for Google
Workspace: Gmail, Drive and Docs, Common Controls, Calendar, Chat, Meet, Groups, Sites, Classroom, Gemini and
Assured Controls.

Each policy is one row, `MP.SCUBA.GWS.<product>.<group>.<policy>`: `GWS.GMAIL.1.1v1` is `MP.SCUBA.GWS.GMAIL.1.1`.
The ID leaves out the policy's version, so a row keeps its ID when CISA updates the policy. Each row has the
policy's requirement as its title, the baseline's rationale, the steps to configure it, its NIST SP 800-53 and
MITRE ATT&CK mappings, and what ScubaGoggles found. Rows are tagged `ScubaGoggles` and `GWS.<product>`
(`GWS.GMAIL`, `GWS.DRIVEDOCS` and so on), and policies that BOD 25-01 requires are tagged `BOD-25-01`.

The pack does not sign in to Google or run ScubaGoggles: you run ScubaGoggles, and the pack reads the results file
it wrote. It needs Maester 3.0 or later.

## Run it

Install ScubaGoggles once, with Python 3.11 or later:

```bash
pip install scubagoggles
scubagoggles setup
```

`scubagoggles setup` downloads [Open Policy Agent](https://www.openpolicyagent.org/), which ScubaGoggles uses to
evaluate the policies, and saves the output folder and the credentials file. ScubaGoggles signs in with a Google
OAuth client and a super admin, or with a service account that has domain-wide delegation; its
[authentication guide](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles/blob/main/docs/authentication/AuthenticationMethods.md)
says how to set up either one.

Run the assessment:

```bash
scubagoggles gws -o ./scubagoggles
```

Install the pack, point it at the output folder in `maester-config.json`, and run it:

```powershell
Install-MtPack maester365/maester-pack-scubagoggles
```

```json
{ "GlobalSettings": { "ScubaGoggles.ReportPath": "./scubagoggles" } }
```

```powershell
Invoke-Maester -Pack SCUBA.GWS -SkipBuiltIn -SkipGraphConnect    # only the ScubaGoggles results
Invoke-Maester                                                   # Maester's tests and the ScubaGoggles results
```

To confirm the install, type the pack's code, `SCUBA.GWS`. Once installed, the pack runs with every
`Invoke-Maester`; without `ScubaGoggles.ReportPath` it reports one skipped row that says what to do.

`ScubaGoggles.ReportPath` takes the `ScubaResults_<uuid>.json` file, the `GWSBaselineConformance_<time>` folder
that one run wrote it in, or the output folder, where the pack reads the newest run. It refuses a report older
than `ScubaGoggles.MaxReportAgeDays` (7 by default; 0 turns the check off), and a results file that another SCuBA
tool, such as ScubaGear, wrote.

Maester does not connect to Google for this pack. `Connect-Maester` is only needed for the other tests you run with
it: when you run the pack on its own, add `-SkipGraphConnect`, or `Invoke-Maester` stops because it is not
connected to Microsoft Graph.

## Run it in a pipeline

Run ScubaGoggles with a service account as its own step, then Maester in the same job:

```yaml
- name: Run ScubaGoggles
  run: |
    pip install scubagoggles
    mkdir -p ~/opa
    # Saves the paths and downloads OPA into ~/opa.
    scubagoggles setup --opapath ~/opa --credentials ./service-account.json --outputpath ./scubagoggles
    scubagoggles gws --subjectemail admin@example.org --quiet

- name: Run Maester
  shell: pwsh
  run: |
    Install-Module Maester -Scope CurrentUser -Force
    Install-MtPack maester365/maester-pack-scubagoggles -Confirm:$false
    Invoke-Maester -Pack SCUBA.GWS -SkipBuiltIn -SkipGraphConnect -NonInteractive -OutputFolder ./test-results
```

Keep the service account key in a pipeline secret, and write it to `service-account.json` in an earlier step. See
the ScubaGoggles [parameters](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles/blob/main/docs/usage/Parameters.md) for
`--subjectemail` and the other options.

## Settings

All settings go in `GlobalSettings` of `maester-config.json`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ScubaGoggles.ReportPath` | empty | The ScubaResults file, the folder one run wrote it in, or the output folder (the newest run is read). |
| `ScubaGoggles.MaxReportAgeDays` | `7` | Refuse a report older than this. `0` turns the check off. |

## How results map

| ScubaGoggles result | Maester result |
| --- | --- |
| Pass | Passed |
| Fail (a SHALL policy) | Failed, High severity |
| Warning (a SHOULD or MAY policy) | Failed, Medium or Low severity |
| No events found | Investigate: a log-based check found no event that shows the setting |
| N/A | Skipped: ScubaGoggles doesn't check the policy, so check it by hand |
| Omitted | Skipped, with the reason from your ScubaGoggles config |
| Incorrect result | Skipped, with what ScubaGoggles reported |
| Error | Error |

The severity follows the policy's criticality whatever the result: SHALL is High, SHOULD is Medium, MAY is Low.

ScubaGoggles writes its own HTML report, `BaselineReports.html`, beside the results file. It is several files, so
the Maester report links to the baselines rather than embedding it; open it from the ScubaGoggles output folder.

## Report an issue

CISA writes and maintains the baselines and ScubaGoggles' checks. If a result, the text of a policy or its steps
look wrong, raise it in [cisagov/ScubaGoggles](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles/issues). Problems with
reading the results in Maester go to [this repository's issues](https://github.com/maester365/maester-pack-scubagoggles/issues).

## Maintaining the pack

`catalog.json` lists the policies of CISA's Google Workspace baselines, with their text, mappings and steps, for
the pack's page on the pack index and for each result's description. It is generated; do not edit it. To move the
pack to a new version of ScubaGoggles, clone that release and run the generator:

```powershell
git clone --depth 1 --branch v1.1.0 https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles ~/src/ScubaGoggles
. ./tools/Update-ScubaGwsCatalog.ps1
Update-ScubaGwsCatalog -SourcePath ~/src/ScubaGoggles
```

The generator reads the baseline Markdown (`scubagoggles/baselines/*.md`), so a change to how CISA writes those
files can drop a field. The pack check ([check-pack.yml](.github/workflows/check-pack.yml)) fails when a policy has
no title, criticality, rationale or remediation. It also runs the pack on `tools/fixtures`, a cut of ScubaGoggles'
sample report with each result ScubaGoggles writes, and fails when one maps to the wrong Maester result. When
ScubaGoggles changes the results it writes (a new `Result` value, say; CISA documents the file in
[tooloutputschema.md](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles/blob/main/docs/misc/tooloutputschema.md)), update
`Test-ScubaGws` in [tests/Test.MP.SCUBA.GWS.ps1](tests/Test.MP.SCUBA.GWS.ps1), the fixture and the check.

Releases work as in the [demo pack](https://github.com/maester365/maester-pack-demo#versions-and-releases): with
the repository variable `PACK_RELEASES` set to `true`, every merged pull request gets the next version and a
release, with its notes from [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). Without it, `Install-MtPack` installs `main`.

## Files

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `maester-pack.json` | The manifest: ID, code, version, the suite, helpers and catalog |
| `maester-pack.guide.json` | How to install and run the pack, for its page on the pack index |
| `catalog.json` | The baselines' policies, generated by `tools/Update-ScubaGwsCatalog.ps1` |
| `tests/` | The suite: the `MP.SCUBA.GWS` family test, with its instance source, and its Markdown |
| `helpers/` | Finding and reading the results file, the catalog, and turning ScubaGoggles' HTML into Markdown |
| `tools/` | The catalog generator and the fixture the pack check runs on. The pack never loads it |

## Licence

This pack is published under the [MIT licence](LICENSE). ScubaGoggles and the SCuBA baselines are published by CISA
under [CC0 1.0](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles/blob/main/LICENSE); the pack does not include ScubaGoggles'
code. `catalog.json` is generated from the baselines, and `tools/fixtures` is cut from ScubaGoggles' sample report.
CISA does not endorse this pack.

    written to maester-packs.lock.json (commit, digest, test IDs, risk and modules) and to the Packs list
    of maester-config.json. Commit both files: Restore-MtPack installs the same files on another computer
    or in a pipeline, and Invoke-Maester runs a pack only while its files still match the lock file.

    A pack that ships with Maester (by ID, such as maester.zero-trust-assessment) needs no approval. Installing it only
    saves and pins the modules it declares.

    For a pack from a public GitHub repository, Maester sends api.maester.dev one anonymous event: the
    pack's source and commit, and a random installation ID. It counts the install and lists the pack. Nothing
    is sent for a private repository or a local folder, or when MAESTER_DISABLE_TELEMETRY is set to 1.
